habits than "auditing app permissions"?
options: The former are tied to actions performed many times daily, while permission audits require deeper, less frequent review
Frequency has no bearing on how habits are categorised in this framework
Auditing app permissions should actually be done more often than verifying payee names
There is no meaningful difference in frequency between these habits
questions.explanation:
The cadence framework matches habit frequency to how often the underlying action naturally occurs and how much
depth of review it requires.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the intended tone of this capstone module compared to the earlier modules in the
category?
options: It contains no reference to real-life scenarios at all
It is more practical and action-oriented, translating prior knowledge into a simple, repeatable routine
It focuses exclusively on advanced legal provisions
It is more technical and detailed than any previous module
questions.explanation:
This module intentionally shifts focus toward practical application, turning the detailed knowledge from earlier modules
into an actionable daily routine.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT one of the four cadences used to organise habits in this module?
options: Daily
Weekly
Yearly
As-Needed✅ Correct Answer: Option C
questions.explanation:
The four cadences used are Daily, Weekly, Monthly, and As-Needed — "Yearly" is not one of the categories, though the
module references annual national campaigns separately.

questions.question: Considering everything in this module, what is its ultimate stated goal?
options: To introduce a completely new set of unrelated cybersecurity threats
To replace the need for any government cybersecurity agency
To provide entertainment value with no practical application
To turn nine modules of knowledge into habits simple enough to sustain for life
questions.explanation: Official JanGyan verified citizen concept.

questions.question: How is India described in Article 1 of the Constitution?
options: A monarchy with elected advisors
A Union of States
A federation of independent nations
A confederation with no central authority
questions.explanation: Article 1 describes India as "a Union of States," reflecting its distinctive, largely indestructible federal structure.

questions.question: What are the three levels of government in India?
options: National and International
Central, Regional, and District only
Central, State, and Local
Federal and Provincial only
questions.explanation:
India's governance operates across Central (Union), State, and Local (Panchayats/Municipalities) levels, each with distinct
responsibilities.

questions.question: What are the three branches of government?
options: President, Governor, and Mayor
Central, State, and Local
Executive, Judiciary, and Media
Legislature, Executive, and Judiciary
questions.explanation: The Legislature makes laws, the Executive implements them, and the Judiciary interprets laws and delivers justice.

questions.question: Who is the ceremonial Head of State at the Central level?
options: The President
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The Chief Justice
The Prime Minister
questions.explanation:
The President serves as India's constitutional Head of State, while real executive power rests with the Prime Minister and
Council of Ministers.

questions.question: Who holds the real executive power at the Union level?
options: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
The Chief Justice of India
The President alone
questions.explanation:
While the President's role is largely ceremonial, the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers exercise the actual executive
authority.

questions.question: What are the two houses of India's Parliament?
options: Rajya Sabha and Vidhan Parishad
Vidhan Sabha and Vidhan Parishad
Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha
Lok Sabha and Vidhan Sabha
questions.explanation: Parliament consists of the Lok Sabha (directly elected) and the Rajya Sabha (representing the states).

questions.question: Who is the ceremonial Head of State at the State level?
options: The District Collector
The Chief Minister
The Speaker of the Vidhan Sabha
The Governor
questions.explanation:
The Governor, appointed by the President, serves as the state-level constitutional head, mirroring the President's role at
the Centre.

questions.question: What establishes the three-tier Panchayati Raj system for rural local government?
options: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment, 1992
The 86th Constitutional Amendment
The 74th Constitutional Amendment, 1992
The 42nd Constitutional Amendment
questions.explanation: The 73rd Amendment of 1992 formally established the modern Panchayati Raj structure across rural India.

questions.question: What establishes urban local bodies like Municipal Corporations?
options: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment
The 74th Constitutional Amendment, 1992
The 44th Constitutional Amendment
The 42nd Constitutional Amendment
questions.explanation: The 74th Amendment of 1992 established the framework for Municipal Corporations, Councils, and Nagar Panchayats.

questions.question: What are the three tiers of the Panchayati Raj system?
options: Municipal Corporation, Council, Nagar Panchayat
Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, Vidhan Sabha
Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti, Zilla Parishad
President, Governor, Mayor
questions.explanation:
Rural local government operates through Gram Panchayat (village), Panchayat Samiti (block), and Zilla Parishad (district)
levels.

questions.question: Which of these is a State List subject, meaning states legislate on it?
options: Foreign affairs
Defence
Currency✅ Correct Answer: Option B
Police
questions.explanation:
Police is a State List subject under the Seventh Schedule, meaning individual states are responsible for legislating and
administering it.

questions.question: Which of these is a Union List subject?
options: Defence
Local government
Agriculture✅ Correct Answer: Option C
Public health
questions.explanation: Defence is a Union List subject, meaning only Parliament has the authority to legislate on it.

questions.question: What does the "Concurrent List" allow?
options: Only the Centre can legislate on these subjects
Both the Centre and States can legislate, with Union law prevailing in conflict
Local bodies exclusively legislate on these subjects
Only states can legislate on these subjects
questions.explanation:
The Concurrent List, covering subjects like education, allows both Centre and States to legislate, with the Union law taking
precedence in case of conflict.

questions.question:
Ramesh has a complaint about a broken streetlight in his neighbourhood. Which level of government should he
approach?
options: His state's chief minister directly
The central government
His local Municipal Corporation or Gram Panchayat
The Supreme Court
questions.explanation:
Streetlights and local infrastructure are local government responsibilities, making the Municipal Corporation or Gram
Panchayat the correct point of contact.

questions.question: Which body would a citizen approach for a passport application?
options: State police department
Local Gram Panchayat
Municipal Corporation
Central Government (Ministry of External Affairs)
questions.explanation: Passports are a Central Government (Union List) subject, handled through the Ministry of External Affairs.

questions.question: What is the "Seventh Schedule" of the Constitution?
options: The section dividing law-making subjects into Union, State, and Concurrent Lists
A list of political parties
A schedule of court holidays
A list of fundamental rights
questions.explanation:
The Seventh Schedule organises legislative subjects into three lists, clarifying which level of government legislates on
what.

questions.question: What is the concept of "checks and balances" meant to prevent?
options: States from having their own governments
Any single branch of government from becoming too powerful
Local bodies from functioning at all
Citizens from voting freely
questions.explanation: Checks and balances ensure that the Legislature, Executive, and Judiciary each limit and are accountable to one another.

questions.question: Can the Judiciary create new laws like the Legislature does?
options: Only High Courts can create laws
Yes, courts frequently create entirely new laws
No, courts interpret and apply laws; law-making is the Legislature's constitutional role
Only the Supreme Court can create laws
questions.explanation:
The Judiciary's role is to interpret and apply existing laws, while the Legislature holds the constitutional authority to make
new laws.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects why some national schemes are described as "designed centrally but implemented
through state and local governments"?
options: Only local governments design and implement schemes
Central schemes never involve states at all
National schemes are always implemented by international agencies
Central funding and guidelines often rely on state and local bodies to actually deliver services to citizens
questions.explanation:
Many centrally sponsored schemes rely on state departments and local bodies for actual delivery, even though policy and
funding originate centrally.

questions.question: Which of the following government levels is typically responsible for birth and death registration?
options: Local government (Municipal Corporation or Gram Panchayat)
The Supreme Court
Central Government
State Government exclusively
questions.explanation:
Birth and death registration is handled at the local government level, making it one of the clearest examples of a purely
local service.

questions.question: Priya wants to file a police complaint about a theft. Which level of government is responsible for police services?
options: Central Government
State Government
Local Government
The judiciary directly, bypassing police entirely
questions.explanation: Police is a State List subject, meaning state governments are responsible for law enforcement and police administration.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the "Legislature"?
options: Interpreting laws and delivering justice
Collecting taxes directly from citizens
Making laws
Implementing and enforcing laws
questions.explanation: The Legislature — Parliament at the Centre and State Legislatures at the state level — is responsible for making laws.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the "Executive"?
options: Conducting elections
Making laws
Interpreting the Constitution exclusively
Implementing and enforcing laws and policies
questions.explanation:
The Executive — the President/Governor, PM/CM, and Council of Ministers — is responsible for implementing and
enforcing laws and policies.

questions.question: Which of these correctly identifies the "Vidhan Sabha"?
options: A state's Legislative Assembly
India's national Parliament
A central government ministry
A type of municipal court
questions.explanation: The Vidhan Sabha is the Legislative Assembly present in every Indian state, forming part of the state legislature.

questions.question: Which urban local body typically governs a large city?
options: Gram Panchayat
Municipal Corporation
Panchayat Samiti
Zilla Parishad
questions.explanation:
Municipal Corporations are the urban local bodies established to govern large cities under the 74th Constitutional
Amendment framework.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects a "myth" about India's government structure, according to standard civics understanding?
options: Local government is generally unimportant
All of the above are accurate myths worth correcting
The Prime Minister personally handles every single government function nationwide
Real administration is distributed across ministries, states, and local bodies
questions.explanation:
It is a common misconception that the PM personally manages everything; in reality, administration is distributed across
many levels and bodies.

questions.question: Why might all centrally sponsored schemes NOT work identically across every state?
options: Because central schemes are illegal in some states
Because only one state is allowed to implement any scheme
Because central schemes have no connection to states at all
Because implementation often varies by state, based on local rules and administrative capacity
questions.explanation:
Even when a scheme is centrally designed, actual implementation can differ across states due to varying local capacity
and rules.

questions.question: Which of these accurately reflects the number of states and Union Territories in India as referenced in this module?
options: 28 states and 8 Union Territories
35 states and 10 Union Territories
20 states and 5 Union Territories
15 states and 2 Union Territories
questions.explanation: India currently comprises 28 states and 8 Union Territories, forming the foundation of its federal structure.

questions.question: What is the correct sequence for a Bill to become a law at the Central level (simplified)?
options: Introduced by the Supreme Court → passed by the Governor
Introduced in a House → debated/passed by both Houses → sent for Presidential assent → becomes an Act
Introduced by a Gram Panchayat → passed by the Municipal Corporation
Presidential assent → introduced in a House → passed by both Houses
questions.explanation:
A Bill must be introduced, debated, and passed by both Houses of Parliament before receiving Presidential assent to
become law.

questions.question: Which government level is generally responsible for ration card issuance and management?
options: The Supreme Court
Local Panchayat exclusively
State Government
Central Government exclusively
questions.explanation: Ration cards are managed at the state level, which is why application processes and portals differ from state to state.

questions.question: What is the primary role of "Zilla Parishad" in the Panchayati Raj structure?
options: National-level governance
Village-level governance
Ward-level governance in cities
District-level governance
questions.explanation: The Zilla Parishad operates at the district level, forming the top tier of the three-tier Panchayati Raj system.

questions.question: Which of these is the correct definition of "federal structure"?
options: Division of governing power across different levels of government
A monarchy-based system of rule
A system where only one level of government exists
A system with no elected officials
questions.explanation:
A federal structure divides governing authority across multiple levels — Central, State, and Local — each with defined
powers.

questions.question: What is "Nagar Panchayat"?
options: A type of central ministry
An urban local body for areas transitioning from rural to urban
A national parliament committee
A rural village council
questions.explanation: Nagar Panchayats govern areas that are transitioning from rural to urban status, distinct from full Municipal Corporations.

questions.question: Which of these best describes "Municipal Council (Nagar Palika)"?
options: A body governing very large metropolitan cities exclusively
A national-level legislative body
An urban local body typically governing smaller cities and towns
A rural-only governance structure
questions.explanation: Municipal Councils, or Nagar Palikas, govern smaller cities and towns, distinct from the larger Municipal Corporations.

questions.question: Which of these correctly identifies "Articles 74 and 75" of the Constitution?
options: They establish the Supreme Court
They establish the Election Commission
They establish state Panchayats
They establish the Council of Ministers at the Union level, headed by the Prime Minister
questions.explanation: Articles 74 and 75 provide the constitutional basis for the Council of Ministers at the Union level, led by the Prime Minister.

questions.question: Which Articles establish the Council of Ministers at the State level?
options: Articles 163 and 164
Articles 124 and 214
Articles 74 and 75
Article 1✅ Correct Answer: Option B
questions.explanation: Articles 163 and 164 establish the State Council of Ministers, headed by the Chief Minister.

questions.question: Which Articles establish the Supreme Court and High Courts respectively?
options: Articles 74 and 75
Article 124 and Article 214
Articles 163 and 164
Articles 1 and 2
questions.explanation: Article 124 establishes the Supreme Court, while Article 214 establishes the High Courts in each state.

questions.question: Anjali is confused whether a government scheme she heard about is centrally or state-run. What is the best approach?
options: Ignore the scheme entirely due to the confusion
Assume it must be entirely central since it was mentioned nationally
Check the scheme's official website or ask a local representative for clarification
Assume all schemes work identically everywhere without checking
questions.explanation:
Verifying through the scheme's official source or a local representative clarifies which level of government is responsible
and how it's implemented locally.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects why local government is sometimes underestimated in importance?
options: Local government has no connection to citizens' daily lives
Local government only exists in rural areas
Local governments have no real functions
Local bodies deliver many of the services citizens interact with most directly, like sanitation and local roads
questions.explanation:
Despite sometimes being overlooked, local bodies handle many day-to-day services that directly affect citizens' quality of
life.

questions.question: What is the correct relationship between the "Executive" and the "Legislature" in terms of accountability?
options: The Executive, including the Council of Ministers, remains accountable to the Legislature
The Executive is never accountable to the Legislature
There is no accountability relationship between the two
The Legislature is accountable to the Executive exclusively
questions.explanation:
The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Legislature (Lok Sabha at the Centre), reflecting the
parliamentary system's accountability structure.

questions.question: Which of these is the correct definition of "Gram Panchayat"?
options: A national-level parliamentary body
The village-level unit of rural local self-government
An urban municipal body
A state high court
questions.explanation: The Gram Panchayat is the foundational village-level unit within the three-tier Panchayati Raj system.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a purely local government responsibility?
options: National defence policy
Issuing passports
Local road maintenance and garbage collection
Setting national interest rates
questions.explanation: Local road maintenance and sanitation are classic examples of services delivered directly by local government bodies.

questions.question: What is the correct way to think about the President's role compared to the Prime Minister's role?
options: Both hold identical executive powers
The Prime Minister has no real power at all
The President has more power than the Prime Minister in all matters
The President's role is largely ceremonial, while the PM and Council of Ministers hold real executive power
questions.explanation:
While the President is the constitutional Head of State, actual governance and policy-making rest with the Prime Minister
and Council of Ministers.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects a common citizen mistake related to government structure?
options: Approaching the wrong level of government for a service, causing delays
Recognising that police is a state subject
Understanding the difference between Central, State, and Local government
Knowing which level of government to approach for a specific issue
questions.explanation:
A common and avoidable mistake is approaching the wrong level of government, which can significantly delay resolution
of an issue.

questions.question:
Which of these accurately reflects the number of Fundamental Duties or amendments relevant to Panchayati Raj
discussed in this module context?
options: Only the 86th Amendment governs local government
The 73rd Amendment (1992) for Panchayati Raj and 74th Amendment (1992) for Urban Local Bodies
Only the 42nd Amendment governs both rural and urban local bodies
There have been no constitutional amendments related to local government
questions.explanation:
The 73rd and 74th Amendments of 1992 are the specific constitutional foundations for rural Panchayati Raj and urban local
bodies respectively.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects appropriate civic engagement at the local level?
options: Assuming local governance has no mechanisms for citizen participation
Only engaging with the central government
Participating in Gram Sabha or ward committee meetings where available
Avoiding all local governance participation
questions.explanation:
Gram Sabha and ward committee meetings are direct mechanisms through which citizens can engage with local
governance.

questions.question: Which of these is the best first step if you're unsure which government office handles your specific concern?
options: Escalate directly to the Prime Minister's office regardless of the issue
Give up on resolving the issue
Assume no government office can help
Ask your local representative or check the National Portal (India.gov.in) for guidance
questions.explanation:
Local representatives and national guidance portals like India.gov.in can help direct citizens to the correct office for their
specific need.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the purpose of "MyGov" and "India.gov.in" as referenced across 
Services category?
options: They are official citizen-facing portals providing verified government information
They are private companies unrelated to government services
They only provide entertainment content
They replace the need for any government structure at all
questions.explanation:
MyGov and India.gov.in serve as official, verified sources of information about government structure, schemes, and services
for citizens.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects why understanding government structure is described as a "practical skill"?
options: It has no real-world application beyond exams
It helps citizens access the right service from the right office efficiently
It is only relevant to government employees
It only matters during election season
questions.explanation:
Understanding which level of government handles which issue directly translates into more efficient, less frustrating
access to public services.

questions.question: Considering everything in this module, what is the central lesson about India's government structure?
options: Government structure is irrelevant to everyday citizen needs
Local government has no meaningful role in citizens' lives
Understanding the three-tier, three-branch structure helps citizens engage effectively and access the right services
All government functions are handled identically by a single central office
questions.explanation:
The central lesson is that understanding India's layered government structure directly empowers citizens to navigate
public services more effectively.

questions.question: Which authority issues the Aadhaar card in India?
options: Ministry of External Affairs
Election Commission of India
Income Tax Department
Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI)
questions.explanation: UIDAI is the statutory authority responsible for issuing and regulating the Aadhaar identity number.

questions.question: How many digits does an Aadhaar number contain?
options: 8✅ Correct Answer: Option B
questions.explanation: Aadhaar is a 12-digit random identity number based on demographic and biometric data.

questions.question: What is "masked Aadhaar"?
options: An Aadhaar copy showing all 12 digits clearly
An Aadhaar copy showing only the last 4 digits
A digital Aadhaar stored only in DigiLocker
An expired Aadhaar card
questions.explanation: Masked Aadhaar hides the first 8 digits, showing only the last 4, offering extra privacy when sharing physical copies.

questions.question: What is PAN primarily used for?
options: Driving a vehicle
Voting in elections
Tracking financial transactions and tax compliance
International travel
questions.explanation:
PAN (Permanent Account Number) is issued by the Income Tax Department to track financial transactions and ensure tax
compliance.

questions.question: How many characters does a PAN number contain?
options: 8-character numeric code
12-digit numeric code
16-character alphanumeric code
10-character alphanumeric code
questions.explanation: PAN consists of a 10-character alphanumeric code issued by the Income Tax Department.

questions.question: What is the "PAN 2.0 Project"?
options: A modernisation project adding QR codes and a unified portal, while keeping existing PAN numbers valid for life
A scheme that abolishes PAN entirely
A private company's PAN verification service
A scheme requiring everyone to reapply for a completely new PAN number
questions.explanation:
PAN 2.0 modernises the PAN system with QR-code verification and a single unified portal, without requiring citizens to
reapply.

questions.question: What does "EPIC" stand for in the context of voter identification?
options: Election Process Identity Card
Electors Photo Identity Card
Electronic Personal Information Card
Employment Proof Identity Card
questions.explanation: EPIC stands for Electors Photo Identity Card, commonly known as the Voter ID, issued by the Election Commission of India.

questions.question: Which authority issues passports in India?
options: Income Tax Department
UIDAI
Ministry of External Affairs (MEA)
State Transport Department
questions.explanation: Passports are issued by the Ministry of External Affairs through the Passport Seva network.

questions.question: What is the "Tatkal" scheme related to?
options: A digital wallet
A type of ration card
A form of voter registration
A faster processing option for urgent passport (and other document) needs
questions.explanation: Tatkal offers expedited processing for urgent document needs, most notably for passport applications.

questions.question: What must an applicant obtain BEFORE a Permanent Driving Licence?
options: A Learner's Licence
A PAN card
A Voter ID
A passport✅ Correct Answer: Option B
questions.explanation: Applicants must first hold a Learner's Licence and pass a road test before receiving a Permanent Driving Licence.

questions.question: Which portal handles Driving Licence applications in India?
options: Passport Seva
Sarathi/Parivahan
voters.eci.gov.in
UIDAI
questions.explanation:
The Sarathi/Parivahan portal, under the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways framework, processes Driving Licence
applications.

questions.question: Within how many days should a birth typically be registered for free registration?
options: 6 months✅ Correct Answer: Option B
1 year
21 days
90 days
questions.explanation:
Births should ideally be registered within 21 days for free registration; delayed registration is possible but may require
additional steps.

questions.question: Which law governs the registration of births and deaths in India?
options: The Passports Act, 1967
The Aadhaar Act, 2016
The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988
The Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969
questions.explanation: The Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969, mandates the registration of these key life events with local authorities.

questions.question: Which law provides the basis for marriage registration, depending on applicable personal law?
options: The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, or the Special Marriage Act, 1954
The Passports Act, 1967
The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988
The Aadhaar Act, 2016
questions.explanation:
Marriage registration is governed by applicable personal law, such as the Hindu Marriage Act or the Special Marriage Act,
depending on the couple's circumstances.

questions.question: What is "One Nation One Ration Card" (ONORC)?
options: A scheme limiting ration cards to a single state
A scheme allowing ration card holders to access subsidised food grains from any Fair Price Shop nationwide
A private company's food delivery service
A scheme that abolishes ration cards
questions.explanation: ONORC enables ration card portability, letting beneficiaries access their entitlements from any Fair Price Shop across India.

questions.question: By when was ONORC fully rolled out across all states and Union Territories?
options: December 2025
It has never been fully rolled out
June 2022
January 2020
questions.explanation: ONORC achieved full rollout across all 28 states and 8 Union Territories by June 2022.

questions.question: What is DigiLocker primarily used for?
options: Booking railway tickets
Filing income tax returns exclusively
Making UPI payments
Storing verified digital copies of government-issued documents
questions.explanation:
DigiLocker is a government-backed digital document wallet, storing officially recognised digital copies of documents like
Driving Licences and mark sheets.

questions.question: Are documents stored in DigiLocker legally valid?
options: Yes, they are accepted at par with physical originals for most official purposes
No, they have no legal standing
Only if printed out first
Only for passport applications
questions.explanation:
DigiLocker documents are officially recognised as equivalent to physical originals for most administrative and legal
purposes.

questions.question: Which of these is classified under "Civil Registration" documents?
options: DigiLocker✅ Correct Answer: Option B
Birth Certificate, Death Certificate, Marriage Certificate
Ration Card only
Aadhaar, PAN, Voter ID
questions.explanation: Birth, death, and marriage certificates fall under civil registration, officially recording key life events.

questions.question: What is a "Virtual ID (VID)"?
options: A permanent replacement for Aadhaar
A digital voter ID
A temporary, revocable 16-digit number used instead of sharing your actual Aadhaar number
A type of driving licence
questions.explanation: The VID offers a safer alternative to sharing your actual Aadhaar number, and can be regenerated as needed.

questions.question:
Vikram wants to prove his identity but is concerned about privacy. What is the safest option when submitting a physical
Aadhaar copy?
options: Share his full Aadhaar number and photo openly
Post his Aadhaar details on social media for verification
Avoid using Aadhaar for identity proof entirely
Use masked Aadhaar, showing only the last 4 digits
questions.explanation: Masked Aadhaar provides sufficient identity verification while protecting the full number from unnecessary exposure.

questions.question: Which document is essential for school admissions and passport applications, among other uses?
options: Birth Certificate
Driving Licence
Ration Card
Marriage Certificate
questions.explanation:
The birth certificate is a foundational document required for school admissions, passports, and many other lifelong
services.

questions.question: What happens if someone holds more than one PAN card?
options: It is required for large businesses
This is not permitted under law
It has no legal implications
This is fully legal and encouraged
questions.explanation: Holding multiple PAN cards is illegal; individuals must have only one PAN.

questions.question: What should you do before selling an old smartphone that contains your accounts and data?
options: Give it away without any preparation
Only delete a few photos
Perform a full factory reset and remove your linked accounts first
Nothing; simply hand it over
questions.explanation: A full factory reset combined with removing linked accounts helps protect your personal data from the next owner.

questions.question: Which document is required to legally drive a motor vehicle in India?
options: Aadhaar card
Ration card
PAN card✅ Correct Answer: Option B
Driving Licence
questions.explanation: A valid Driving Licence, issued by the State Transport Department, is legally required to drive a motor vehicle.

questions.question: Which government portal is used for voter registration in India?
options: voters.eci.gov.in
passportindia.gov.in
incometax.gov.in
uidai.gov.in
questions.explanation: The National Voters' Service Portal, voters.eci.gov.in, is the official platform for voter registration and related services.

questions.question: What percentage of India's adult population is estimated to be enrolled in Aadhaar?
options: About 10%✅ Correct Answer: Option B
About 99%
About 25%
About 50%
questions.explanation:
Aadhaar enrolment covers approximately 99% of India's adult population, making it the world's largest biometric identity
system.

questions.question: What should you do if your name is spelled differently across your Aadhaar, PAN, and Voter ID?
options: Assume only the government needs to worry about this
Ignore the discrepancy, since it has no consequences
Get the details corrected to be consistent, as mismatches can cause issues in official processes
Create a fourth document with a completely different spelling
questions.explanation:
Consistent name and date-of-birth spelling across documents helps avoid complications during verification for various
official processes.

questions.question: Which of these documents is typically required for opening a bank account or applying for a loan?
options: Ration card exclusively
Voter ID exclusively
Marriage certificate exclusively
PAN card
questions.explanation: PAN is commonly required for significant financial transactions, including opening bank accounts and applying for loans.

questions.question: What is the correct definition of "e-KYC"?
options: Electronic identity verification, typically using Aadhaar
A method of paying electricity bills
A type of physical document storage
A government tax refund process
questions.explanation: e-KYC enables quick, paperless identity verification using Aadhaar-based authentication.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects a myth about ration cards addressed in this module?
options: Under ONORC, ration cards work at any Fair Price Shop across India
Ration cards only work in the cardholder's home state
Ration cards are linked to Aadhaar
Ration cards support the Public Distribution System

This is a myth; under ONORC, ration cards are portable and usable at any Fair Price Shop nationwide, not just in the home
state.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects a common mistake related to identity documents?
options: Registering a birth within 21 days
Using masked Aadhaar for physical copies
Posting Aadhaar, PAN, or passport copies publicly on social media
Renewing a passport before it expires
questions.explanation:
Publicly posting identity document copies is a common and risky mistake that can expose citizens to identity theft or
fraud.

questions.question: What should a family do before a child's school admission, related to identity documents?
options: Apply for a Voter ID for the child
Apply for a Driving Licence for the child
Nothing is needed
Ensure the child's birth certificate is registered
questions.explanation: A registered birth certificate is a foundational document typically required for school admissions.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects why PAN is described as valid "for life"?
options: Once issued, PAN generally does not need reapplication regardless of address changes
PAN must be reissued every time you change jobs
PAN must be renewed every 5 years
PAN expires after 10 years
questions.explanation:
Unlike some other documents, PAN remains valid for life; only updates like address changes need to be made, not
reapplication.

questions.question: Which of these best describes the purpose of "Aadhaar Authentication History"?
options: A record of your bank balance
A feature letting you check when and where your Aadhaar was used for authentication
A list of your voting history
A record of your driving violations
questions.explanation:
Checking your Aadhaar Authentication History helps you spot any unauthorised or unfamiliar use of your Aadhaar for
verification.

questions.question: Which of these is the correct process order for obtaining a new Aadhaar card?
options: Apply only online with no biometric requirement
Receive Aadhaar letter first, then visit an enrolment centre

Visit an enrolment centre with ID/address proof, complete biometric capture, then receive the Aadhaar letter after
processing
Aadhaar is issued automatically at birth with no application needed
questions.explanation:
Aadhaar enrolment requires visiting a centre in person for document submission and biometric capture before the
Aadhaar letter is issued.

questions.question: What is a key advantage of the "PAN 2.0" unified portal?
options: It eliminates PAN entirely in favour of Aadhaar
It requires citizens to pay a large reapplication fee
It removes online PAN services altogether
It consolidates three separate PAN service portals into one, with QR-code verification
questions.explanation: PAN 2.0 simplifies PAN services by unifying multiple portals into one and adding secure QR-code verification.

questions.question: Which government ministry oversees Driving Licence standards through the Sarathi/Parivahan framework?
options: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
Ministry of External Affairs
Ministry of Home Affairs
Ministry of Finance
questions.explanation:
The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways oversees Driving Licence standards and the Sarathi/Parivahan digital
platform.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct handling of a deceased family member's affairs regarding documents?
options: No registration or documentation is needed
Register the death with the local Registrar, ideally within 21 days, for use in settling inheritance and other matters
Only a lawyer can register a death
Death registration is optional and rarely necessary
questions.explanation:
Registering a death promptly provides the official documentation needed for inheritance, insurance, and other legal
processes.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects safe practice when applying for any of these documents online?
options: Use unofficial third-party websites for convenience
Share your Aadhaar OTP with any website requesting it
Apply only through official government portals (uidai.gov.in, incometax.gov.in, etc.)
Skip document verification steps entirely
questions.explanation: Applying only through verified official portals protects you from fraudulent websites attempting to collect personal data.

questions.question: Which of these is the correct definition of "digital identity," as covered in this module?
options: A single password used across all accounts
A physical ID card only
Only your Aadhaar number
The complete online representation built from your combined government IDs, profiles, and behaviour
questions.explanation: Digital identity encompasses the full combination of your data points online, extending beyond any single document.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects why "Importance of Digital Identity" is included alongside physical documents in this
module?
options:
India's identity ecosystem increasingly relies on verified digital equivalents like DigiLocker, alongside physical
documents
Digital identity has completely replaced all physical documents
Digital identity only applies to businesses, not individuals
Digital identity has no real-world relevance
questions.explanation:
As India's identity ecosystem evolves, understanding both physical documents and their verified digital equivalents is
increasingly essential.

questions.question: What is the correct definition of "Fair Price Shop" in the context of ration cards?
options: A discount electronics store
A shop distributing subsidised food grains under the Public Distribution System
A private bank branch
A government tax office
questions.explanation:
Fair Price Shops are the designated outlets through which ration card holders access subsidised food grains under the
PDS.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects appropriate action if you're moving states for work and rely on your ration card?
options: Give up your ration card benefits permanently
Assume ration cards cannot be used outside your home district
Rely on ONORC, which allows your existing ration card to work at Fair Price Shops nationwide
Apply for an entirely new ration card in the new state
questions.explanation:
Thanks to ONORC, migrant workers can continue accessing their ration entitlements from any Fair Price Shop across India
without a new card.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct approach to renewing time-bound documents like passports and Driving
Licences?
options: Assume these documents never expire
Only renew if requested by a government office
Wait until they expire before taking any action
Renew well before expiry, especially before planned travel
questions.explanation: Proactively renewing before expiry avoids last-minute complications, especially when travel or driving plans are involved.

questions.question: Which of these is the correct description of "UIDAI"?
options: The Unique Identification Authority of India, which issues Aadhaar
A private data broker
A state transport department
A banking regulator
questions.explanation:
UIDAI is the statutory government body specifically responsible for Aadhaar enrolment, updates, and authentication
standards.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects a responsible habit for managing multiple identity documents?
options: Keep no record of which documents need renewal
Maintain a personal checklist of documents and their renewal timelines
Store all documents only as physical copies with no digital backup
Assume all documents renew themselves automatically
questions.explanation: Maintaining a personal renewal checklist helps prevent documents like passports and licences from lapsing unexpectedly.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the appropriate response to an SMS claiming your Aadhaar will be deactivated unless you
click a link?
options: Reply with your Aadhaar number to confirm
Click the link immediately to prevent deactivation
Ignore the link and verify your Aadhaar status directly via the official UIDAI website or app
Share the link with others to verify collectively
questions.explanation: Such messages are a common fraud pattern; verifying directly through official UIDAI channels avoids falling for the scam.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the overall theme connecting Aadhaar, PAN, Voter ID, Passport, Driving Licence, and civil
registration documents?
options: These documents are only relevant to government employees
They are unrelated and serve no combined purpose
Only Aadhaar has any real significance among these documents
Together, they form the backbone of how citizens prove identity, access services, and exercise rights
questions.explanation: Collectively, these documents enable citizens to establish identity, access services, and exercise their legal and civic rights.

questions.question: Considering everything in this module, what is the most important overall takeaway about citizen identity documents?
options:
Knowing each document's purpose, issuing authority, and how to protect it turns bureaucracy into a manageable
system
Documents should be obtained but never protected or monitored afterward
Digital identity has completely eliminated the need for physical documents
Only one document is ever necessary for any citizen
questions.explanation:
Understanding the purpose, issuing authority, and protection measures for each document empowers citizens to navigate
essential services confidently.

questions.question: What is UMANG?
options: A type of antivirus software
A unified mobile app giving citizens access to thousands of government services in one place
A private banking app
A social media platform
questions.explanation:
UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) aggregates services from central and state departments
into a single app.

questions.question: When was UMANG launched?
options: 1 July 2015
26 July 2014
23 November 2017
28 August 2014
questions.explanation: UMANG was launched on 23 November 2017 by MeitY and the National e-Governance Division (NeGD).

questions.question: Approximately how many services does UMANG host?
options: About 500,000
About 10
About 50
About 1,745
questions.explanation:
UMANG hosts approximately 1,745 services from around 80 central bodies and 30 states, making it a comprehensive
service aggregator.

questions.question: What is MyGov primarily designed for?
options: Enabling citizen participation in governance through ideas, feedback, discussions, and polls
Issuing passports
Filing income tax returns exclusively
Booking railway tickets
questions.explanation:
MyGov is India's citizen engagement platform, allowing people to contribute directly to policy discussions and
government initiatives.

questions.question: When was MyGov launched?
options: 15 August 2019
26 July 2014
23 November 2017
1 July 2015
questions.explanation: MyGov was launched on 26 July 2014 as India's official citizen engagement platform.

questions.question: What is "e-Sign"?
options: A physical signature scanned into a computer
A type of antivirus feature
An Aadhaar-based electronic signature service with the same legal validity as a handwritten signature
A biometric lock for smartphones
questions.explanation:
e-Sign uses Aadhaar authentication (OTP or biometric) to legally sign documents electronically, with the same validity as
handwritten signatures.

questions.question: Which section of the IT Act, 2000, provides legal recognition for electronic signatures like e-Sign?
options: Section 43A
Section 66C
Section 72✅ Correct Answer: Option B
Section 3A
questions.explanation:
Section 3A of the IT Act, 2000, specifically provides legal recognition for electronic signatures, including Aadhaar-based e-
Sign.

questions.question: Which of these documents CANNOT be executed using e-Sign?
options: A will
A standard government form
An insurance policy document
A loan agreement
questions.explanation:
Wills, along with negotiable instruments (other than cheques) and property powers of attorney, are excluded from e-Sign
and require traditional signatures.

questions.question: Who regulates e-Sign service providers in India?
options: UIDAI exclusively
Controller of Certifying Authorities (CCA)
Election Commission of India
Reserve Bank of India
questions.explanation: The CCA, under MeitY, regulates Certifying Authorities and e-Sign service providers in India.

questions.question: What is "India Stack"?
options: A type of mobile phone
A private company's cloud storage service
Shared digital public infrastructure — identity, payments, and data frameworks — that other services build upon
A pile of government forms
questions.explanation:
India Stack refers to foundational shared digital infrastructure like Aadhaar and UPI, which other applications and services
build upon.

questions.question: When was Digital India launched?
options: 26 July 2014
15 August 2019
23 November 2017
1 July 2015
questions.explanation:
Digital India was launched on 1 July 2015 as the umbrella programme under which platforms like UMANG and DigiLocker
were built.

questions.question: What is "G2C" in the context of government services?
options: Government-to-Citizen
Government-to-Global
Government-to-Corporation
Government-to-Currency
questions.explanation:
G2C refers to digital services delivered directly from government bodies to individual citizens, like most platforms covered
in this module.

questions.question: Which of these is the safest way to verify a government website is genuine?
options: Assume all sites with "government" in the name are genuine
Check that it ends in .gov.in or .nic.in
Trust any site appearing in a search engine ad
Judge it purely by its visual design
questions.explanation:
Verifying the exact domain ending — .gov.in or .nic.in — is the most reliable way to confirm a government website's
authenticity.

questions.question: What is a common way UMANG can be accessed besides the mobile app?
options: Only through a fax machine
UMANG has no alternative access channels
Via web, SMS, and IVR (phone call) channels
Only through a physical government office
questions.explanation:
UMANG offers multiple access channels — app, web, SMS, and IVR — making it accessible even without constant internet
access.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects why citizens should never share an OTP used for e-Sign or e-KYC?
options: OTPs for e-Sign expire immediately and cannot be misused
Sharing it has no security implications
Only businesses need to worry about OTP sharing
OTPs authorise sensitive actions, and sharing them, even with someone claiming to help, risks fraud
questions.explanation:
OTPs for e-Sign or e-KYC authorise significant actions, and sharing them with anyone — even someone claiming to assist
— creates serious fraud risk.

questions.question: Rohan receives a WhatsApp message with a link claiming "urgent PAN verification required." What should he do?
options: Ignore it and verify his PAN status directly via the official Income Tax e-filing portal
Reply with his PAN number to confirm
Forward the link to family members without any warning
Click the link immediately to avoid any PAN issues
questions.explanation: Fraudulent "verification" links are a common scam; verifying independently through the official portal avoids falling victim.

questions.question: Which of these best describes MyGov's language accessibility?
options: It operates in only 2 languages
It operates in 12 languages
It is available only in English
It has no regional language support
questions.explanation: MyGov operates in 12 languages, broadening its accessibility to citizens across India's linguistic diversity.

questions.question:
What is the correct definition of a "Consent Manager" as it relates to India's digital ecosystem (referenced alongside
these services)?
options: A type of firewall
A government minister
A registered, independent platform through which individuals manage data-sharing consents
A bank employee handling loans
questions.explanation:
Consent Managers allow individuals to give, review, or withdraw consent for how their data is shared across digital
platforms.

questions.question: Which of these best represents a legitimate use case for UMANG?
options: Applying for a passport at a foreign embassy
Purchasing shares on the stock market
Filing a criminal case directly with a magistrate
Checking your EPFO Provident Fund balance without visiting an office
questions.explanation:
Checking EPFO balances is one of UMANG's most heavily used services, letting citizens avoid physical office visits for this
common need.

questions.question: Which of these is the correct process for e-Signing a document?
options: Upload the document, enter Aadhaar/VID, verify via OTP, and a digital signature certificate is applied
Ask a bank employee to sign on your behalf
Simply type your name at the bottom of a PDF
Print, physically sign, and scan the document
questions.explanation:
e-Sign relies on Aadhaar-based OTP verification to issue a one-time digital signature certificate and apply your legally valid
signature.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the purpose of DigiLocker within the broader digital government ecosystem?
options: It is used exclusively for filing taxes
It provides a secure, officially recognised digital wallet for storing government-issued documents
It is a private company unrelated to government services
It replaces the need for Aadhaar entirely
questions.explanation:
DigiLocker functions as a secure, government-backed digital document wallet, complementing other platforms like
UMANG and e-Sign.

questions.question: What should you do if a "government scheme" WhatsApp message asks for a registration fee?
options: Share your bank OTP to complete registration faster
Assume all scheme-related messages are automatically genuine
Recognise this as a common fraud pattern, since genuine schemes rarely require registration fees
Pay immediately since it may be a limited-time offer
questions.explanation:
Fraudulent scheme-registration fee requests are a well-documented scam pattern; genuine government schemes
typically don't require such fees.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the National e-Governance Division's (NeGD) role?
options: It issues passports
It regulates banking services
It conducts national elections
It develops and maintains platforms like UMANG as part of the Digital India programme
questions.explanation: NeGD, alongside MeitY, is responsible for developing and maintaining major digital government platforms like UMANG.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects a "Departmental Portal" as distinct from a "Service Aggregator" like UMANG?
options:
A departmental portal, like Passport Seva, is dedicated to a single department's services, while UMANG aggregates
many departments
Departmental portals only exist for banking
Service aggregators cannot include any single-department services
They are identical concepts with no difference
questions.explanation:
Departmental portals like Passport Seva serve one specific function, while UMANG aggregates services across numerous
departments in a single app.

questions.question: What percentage growth or scale does UMANG's cumulative transactions reportedly reflect?
options: Exactly 100 transactions
Over 383 crore cumulative transactions
Only about 1,000 transactions
Fewer than 10,000 transactions
questions.explanation: UMANG has processed over 383 crore cumulative transactions, reflecting its massive adoption across Indian citizens.

questions.question: Which of these correctly identifies the legal basis making e-Sign equivalent to a handwritten signature?
options: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019
The Aadhaar Act alone, with no IT Act connection
Section 5 of the IT Act, 2000
There is no legal basis; it's just a convention
questions.explanation: Section 5 of the IT Act, 2000, grants electronic signatures the same legal validity as handwritten signatures.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects safe practice when downloading UMANG, DigiLocker, or MyGov apps?
options: Download via a link shared in an unsolicited SMS
App source doesn't matter for government apps
Download from any third-party app store for convenience
Download only from official app stores, verifying the publisher is MeitY/NeGD or the relevant ministry
questions.explanation:
Verifying the official publisher when downloading from legitimate app stores helps avoid fake, malicious versions of these
government apps.

questions.question: Which of these is the correct definition of a "Departmental Portal" example given in this module?
options: Passport Seva
DigiLocker
UMANG
MyGov
questions.explanation:
Passport Seva is a dedicated departmental portal specifically for passport-related services under the Ministry of External
Affairs.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects why keeping your Aadhaar-linked mobile number updated matters across these digital
platforms?
options: Aadhaar-linked numbers never need updating
Most digital services (UMANG, DigiLocker, e-Sign) depend on OTP verification tied to that number
It only matters for banking services, not government platforms
It has no real impact on service access
questions.explanation:
Since OTP verification underpins most of these services, an outdated Aadhaar-linked mobile number can disrupt access
across multiple platforms.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of "Digital India" as a programme?
options: A private telecom company's marketing campaign
A single app with no broader framework
An umbrella programme, launched in 2015, under which platforms like UMANG and DigiLocker were built
A programme exclusively for urban areas
questions.explanation:
Digital India serves as the overarching government programme encompassing broadband connectivity, e-governance,
and platforms like UMANG.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects a responsible approach to citizen engagement on MyGov?
options: Impersonate other users on the platform
Post spam content unrelated to governance discussions
Avoid using the platform's features altogether
Contribute genuine ideas, feedback, and participate constructively in polls/discussions
questions.explanation:
Responsible digital citizenship on MyGov means contributing genuinely and constructively to the platform's civic
engagement purpose.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects why e-Sign is considered convenient for banking and insurance processes?
options: It eliminates the need for printing, physically signing, and scanning, while remaining legally binding
It requires printing and scanning documents each time
It works only for cash transactions
It has no legal standing, so it's used only informally
questions.explanation:
e-Sign streamlines document signing for banking and insurance by removing physical paperwork steps while maintaining
full legal validity.

questions.question: Which government platform would be most appropriate for tracking the status of a passport application?
options: DigiLocker✅ Correct Answer: Option B
Passport Seva
MyGov
UMANG exclusively
questions.explanation:
Passport Seva is the Ministry of External Affairs' dedicated portal for passport applications, appointments, and status
tracking.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct definition of "Authentication/Signature Service" platforms, as categorised in this
module?
options: DigiLocker exclusively
UMANG and MyGov
e-Sign and Aadhaar authentication
Passport Seva and Income Tax e-Filing
questions.explanation:
e-Sign and Aadhaar authentication are specifically categorised as identity verification and signature services within the
digital government ecosystem.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects appropriate verification before trusting a scheme-related claim seen on social media?
options: Share personal banking details to "confirm" eligibility
Trust it immediately if it mentions a real ministry's name
Assume all social media claims about schemes are accurate
Verify directly on the scheme's official portal or via UMANG before proceeding
questions.explanation:
Independent verification through official channels protects against fraudsters who reference real scheme names to
appear credible.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct sequence for accessing a service through UMANG?
options: Log in with Aadhaar-linked mobile/OTP, search for the service, complete the request within the app
Visit a physical office first, then use UMANG only for confirmation
UMANG requires a separate paid subscription for each service
UMANG cannot process any complete service request
questions.explanation:
UMANG allows users to log in via Aadhaar-linked mobile and OTP, then search for and complete service requests directly
within the app.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the relationship between Aadhaar authentication and the platforms covered in this
module?
options: Aadhaar has been phased out from all digital government platforms
Aadhaar authentication serves as the identity backbone for DigiLocker, UMANG, and e-Sign
None of these platforms use Aadhaar authentication
Only MyGov uses Aadhaar authentication
questions.explanation: Aadhaar-based authentication underpins the identity verification process across DigiLocker, UMANG, and e-Sign.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the risk of downloading government-labelled apps from unofficial sources?
options: Government apps cannot be faked
Unofficial sources are always faster and safer
Fake or malicious apps can impersonate genuine government services to steal data
There is no risk since all apps with government names are genuine
questions.explanation:
Malicious apps sometimes impersonate legitimate government services; downloading only from verified official sources
reduces this risk.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct scope of MyGov's functionality?
options: Only displaying government announcements with no interaction
Exclusively issuing identity documents
Exclusively processing tax refunds
Discussions, tasks, polls, quizzes, blogs, and pledges enabling direct citizen participation
questions.explanation:
MyGov offers a range of interactive features — discussions, polls, quizzes, and more — enabling genuine citizen
participation in governance.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of "Significant Data Fiduciary" obligations, as relevant to large
digital platforms?
options:
Organisations processing data at large scale or high sensitivity face extra obligations like appointing a Data Protection
Officer
Only small businesses face additional obligations
No additional obligations apply regardless of scale
This concept applies only to state governments
questions.explanation:
Large-scale digital platforms handling significant personal data may be classified as Significant Data Fiduciaries, facing
extra compliance obligations under the DPDP Act.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects a citizen's correct understanding of "e-Sign limitations"?
options: e-Sign can be used for absolutely any legal document without exception
Certain documents like wills and property powers of attorney require traditional signatures instead
e-Sign can only be used for government forms
e-Sign has no limitations whatsoever
questions.explanation:
While broadly useful, e-Sign has specific legal exceptions, including wills and property powers of attorney, requiring
traditional signatures.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct role of the Controller of Certifying Authorities (CCA)?
options: Managing India's railway network
Conducting national elections
Regulating e-Sign service providers and Certifying Authorities under the IT Act
Issuing Aadhaar cards
questions.explanation:
The CCA, under MeitY, is specifically responsible for regulating the certifying authorities and e-Sign providers operating in
India.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects why bookmarking official government portals is recommended?
options: Bookmarking makes websites load faster automatically
Bookmarking has no security benefit
It is required by law for all citizens
It avoids the risk of landing on a fraudulent look-alike site through repeated searching
questions.explanation:
Bookmarking official portals reduces the chance of accidentally clicking a fraudulent look-alike link found through casual
searching.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct definition of "Online Government Portal" verification, as taught in this module?
options: Confirming the domain ends in .gov.in or .nic.in before entering personal information
Assuming all portals with "India" in the name are genuine
Verification is unnecessary for government portals
Trusting any portal that appears professional
questions.explanation:
The domain check remains the most reliable method for confirming a government portal's authenticity before sharing any
personal data.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects why the DPDP Act, 2023, is relevant to digital government platforms covered in this
module?
options: It has no relevance to these platforms

It requires reasonable security safeguards for personal data processed through platforms like DigiLocker, UMANG, and
MyGov
It exclusively governs international data transfers
It only applies to private companies, never government platforms
questions.explanation:
The DPDP Act's security safeguard requirements apply to personal data processed by digital government platforms as
much as private ones.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct process to follow if a UMANG service transaction fails or shows an error?
options: Assume nothing can be done and abandon the service entirely
Contact an unofficial "UMANG agent" found online
Check the transaction/status tracking within UMANG itself, since it typically provides tracking and notifications
Immediately uninstall the app without checking further
questions.explanation:
UMANG typically provides in-app tracking and notifications, making it the appropriate first step to check before escalating
further.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct relationship between "National Digital Platforms" and individual citizen
services?
options: National platforms and individual services are entirely separate topics
Only banks benefit from national digital platforms
National platforms have no bearing on how individual services function
Individual services like DigiLocker and UMANG are built upon shared national digital infrastructure like India Stack
questions.explanation:
Citizen-facing services rely on the shared underlying infrastructure of India Stack, illustrating the connection between
broad national platforms and specific services.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects a responsible digital citizenship practice specific to using government platforms?
options: Keeping your own information accurate and never impersonating others on citizen engagement platforms
Sharing your login credentials with others for convenience
Ignoring platform terms of service entirely
Submitting false information on government portals
questions.explanation:
Responsible digital citizenship means maintaining accurate information and never misusing platforms to impersonate
others, which is also a legal offence.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the overall benefit of India's digital government ecosystem, as covered in this module?
options: It only benefits government employees, not ordinary citizens

It brings dozens of once-physical government processes onto citizens' phones, saving time when used correctly and
safely
It has replaced the need for any citizen awareness or safety practices
It has no measurable impact on citizen convenience
questions.explanation:
Platforms like DigiLocker, UMANG, and e-Sign collectively transform previously physical, time-consuming processes into
convenient digital ones.

questions.question: Considering everything in this module, what is the most important overall lesson about digital government services?
options: Trusting every platform blindly regardless of verification
Digital government services require no security awareness at all

Knowing the genuine platforms, using them via official channels, and never sharing OTPs turns this infrastructure into
real, safe convenience
Avoiding all digital government services to eliminate risk
questions.explanation:
The central lesson is that combining awareness of genuine platforms with safe usage habits unlocks the real convenience
of India's digital government ecosystem.

questions.question: Which part of the Constitution contains the Fundamental Rights?
options: Part IVA✅ Correct Answer: Option B
Part IV
Part II
Part III
questions.explanation: Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III (Articles 12-35) of the Constitution, and are directly enforceable in court.

questions.question: Which part of the Constitution contains the Fundamental Duties?
options: Part IVA
Part III
Part V✅ Correct Answer: Option C
Part IV
questions.explanation: Fundamental Duties are listed in Part IVA (Article 51A), added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment.

questions.question: Are Directive Principles of State Policy directly enforceable in court?
options: Yes, exactly like Fundamental Rights
No, but courts often use them to interpret laws and give meaning to other rights
Only state courts can enforce them
Only the Supreme Court can enforce them
questions.explanation:
Directive Principles guide government policy but are not directly enforceable, unlike the legally binding Fundamental
Rights.

questions.question: How many Fundamental Duties are listed under Article 51A?
options: 3✅ Correct Answer: Option B
questions.explanation: Article 51A lists 11 Fundamental Duties, with the 11th added later by the 86th Constitutional Amendment in 2002.

questions.question: Which constitutional amendment originally added the Fundamental Duties?
options: 73rd Amendment, 1992
44th Amendment, 1978
86th Amendment, 2002
42nd Amendment, 1976
questions.explanation: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment of 1976 introduced Fundamental Duties into the Constitution.

questions.question: Which amendment added the 11th Fundamental Duty regarding children's education?
options: 86th Amendment, 2002
42nd Amendment
74th Amendment
73rd Amendment
questions.explanation:
The 86th Amendment of 2002 added the duty for parents/guardians to provide education opportunities for children aged
6-14.

questions.question: Which Fundamental Right is described by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as the "heart and soul" of the Constitution?
options: Cultural and Educational Rights
Right to Constitutional Remedies
Right to Equality
Right to Freedom of Religion
questions.explanation:
Article 32, the Right to Constitutional Remedies, allows citizens to directly approach courts to enforce their Fundamental
Rights.

questions.question: Within how many days must a public authority typically respond to an RTI request?
options: 90 days
7 days
30 days
1 year✅ Correct Answer: Option B
questions.explanation: The Right to Information Act, 2005, requires public authorities to respond to requests within 30 days.

questions.question: What are the six consumer rights guaranteed under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019?
options: Only the right to file a court case
Speed, price, quality, and design
Only the right to a refund
Safety, information, choice, being heard, redressal, and consumer education
questions.explanation: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019, guarantees six specific rights, ensuring comprehensive protection for consumers.

questions.question: What is "e-Jagriti"?
options: India's unified online consumer grievance redressal portal, launched January 2025
A voter registration platform
A police complaint system
A tax filing portal
questions.explanation: e-Jagriti unifies earlier consumer grievance systems into one portal, launched in January 2025.

questions.question: Which body established under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, investigates human rights violations?
options: Central Consumer Protection Authority
National Human Rights Commission (NHRC)
Election Commission of India
UIDAI
questions.explanation:
NHRC, along with State Human Rights Commissions, is empowered to investigate and address human rights violations in
India.

questions.question: Which law provides civil remedies against domestic violence?
options: The POCSO Act, 2012
The Consumer Protection Act, 2019
The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
The RTI Act, 2005
questions.explanation: This 2005 Act specifically provides civil remedies and protection orders for victims of domestic violence.

questions.question: What does POCSO stand for?
options: Public Officer's Code of Service Obligations
Protection of Citizens' Social Order
Protection of Consumer Standards Organisation
Protection of Children from Sexual Offences
questions.explanation: The POCSO Act, 2012, provides special legal protection for children against sexual abuse and exploitation.

questions.question: Which statutory body safeguards women's rights in India?
options: National Commission for Women (NCW)
National Human Rights Commission
Central Consumer Protection Authority
Reserve Bank of India
questions.explanation: The NCW, established in 1992, is the statutory body dedicated to safeguarding women's rights and interests.

questions.question: Which statutory body safeguards children's rights in India?
options: NHRC
NCPCR (National Commission for Protection of Child Rights)
NCW
CCPA✅ Correct Answer: Option A
questions.explanation: NCPCR, established in 2007, focuses specifically on protecting the rights of children in India.

questions.question: Under the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007, senior citizens are defined as those aged:
options: 50 and above
65 and above✅ Correct Answer: Option B
60 and above
70 and above
questions.explanation: The Act defines senior citizens as individuals aged 60 and above, entitled to seek maintenance from children/relatives.

questions.question: What was the original cap on monthly maintenance under the Senior Citizens Act, 2007?
options: ₹1 lakh
There was no cap at all
questions.explanation:
The original Act capped monthly maintenance at ₹10,000, though later amendments have sought to remove this fixed
cap.

questions.question: Where can a senior citizen seek a maintenance order against neglectful children or relatives?
options: A State-constituted Maintenance Tribunal
A private bank
The Election Commission
The Ministry of Railways
questions.explanation: Senior citizens can approach a State Maintenance Tribunal, established under the 2007 Act, to seek a maintenance order.

questions.question: Which of these is an example of a Union List subject under the Seventh Schedule?
options: Police
Defence
Local government
Agriculture
questions.explanation: Defence is a Union List subject, meaning only the central Parliament has authority to legislate on it.

questions.question: Which of these correctly describes the RTI Act's core purpose?
options: To manage India's railway network
To provide free food grains to citizens
To give citizens the legal right to request information from public authorities
To regulate stock market investments
questions.explanation:
The RTI Act, 2005, empowers citizens to request information held by public authorities, promoting government
transparency.

questions.question:
Priya files an RTI request asking why a government decision was made, rather than requesting specific records. What is
the likely issue?
options: RTI can only be used by journalists
This is a perfectly valid RTI use
RTI requests cannot exceed 100 words
RTI applies to factual records/information, not requests for opinions or justifications
questions.explanation: RTI is designed to access existing information/records, not to demand explanations or opinions about decisions.

questions.question: How many RTI applications have reportedly been filed in India since the Act came into force in 2005?
options: Over 2.5 crore
Exactly 1 lakh✅ Correct Answer: Option B
About 500
About 10,000
questions.explanation: Over 2.5 crore RTI applications have been filed since 2005, reflecting its widespread use as a transparency tool.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects a consumer's correct first step before filing a formal complaint?
options: Post about it on social media before any other action
Attempt to resolve the issue directly with the seller/service provider first
Contact the Election Commission
File a court case immediately
questions.explanation:
Attempting direct resolution first is the recommended initial step before escalating to formal consumer complaint
channels.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the "Right to be Heard," one of the six consumer rights?
options: The right to sue for damages exclusively
The right to avoid all consumer transactions
The right to have your grievances properly considered
The right to remain silent during a complaint process
questions.explanation: The "Right to be Heard" ensures that consumer grievances are given genuine consideration during the redressal process.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct scope of the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA)?
options: It has no enforcement powers at all
It only regulates banking services
It only handles voter registration
It can act against misleading advertisements and unfair trade practices, including "dark patterns"
questions.explanation:
The CCPA enforces consumer protection law, including recent action against manipulative "dark pattern" tactics used by
e-commerce platforms.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects appropriate action if you witness a human rights violation by a public official?
options: File a complaint with the NHRC or the relevant State Human Rights Commission
Only discuss it informally with friends
Ignore it completely
Assume no authority can address this
questions.explanation: The NHRC and State Human Rights Commissions are the appropriate bodies to formally address human rights violations.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects a myth about Directive Principles addressed in this module?
options: Courts use them to interpret legislation
They can be enforced in court exactly like Fundamental Rights
They guide government policy
They are found in Part IV of the Constitution
questions.explanation:
This is a myth; unlike Fundamental Rights, Directive Principles are not directly enforceable in court, though courts do
reference them in interpretation.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects why a senior citizen's property transfer to a child might be reversed by courts?
options: Property transfers can never be reversed under any circumstances
Only the government can reverse property transfers
If made conditional on care/maintenance and that condition isn't honoured, courts have upheld reversal
Property transfers are automatically void after one year
questions.explanation:
Courts have upheld that conditional property transfers can be reversed if the senior citizen's welfare, as agreed, isn't
honoured.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects a citizen's Fundamental Duty under Article 51A?
options: To vote in every single election without exception
To join the armed forces
To pay for all government services personally
To protect the natural environment, including forests and wildlife
questions.explanation: Protecting the natural environment, forests, and wildlife is explicitly listed among the 11 Fundamental Duties.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct relationship between "Rights" and "Duties" as framed in this module?
options: Rights protect citizens, while duties bind them to their fellow citizens; together they form a complete civic relationship
They are entirely unrelated concepts
Only duties matter; rights are irrelevant
Only rights matter; duties are irrelevant
questions.explanation:
This module frames rights and duties as two connected halves of the same constitutional relationship between citizens
and the state.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct scope of "human rights" as covered in this module?
options: Rights that apply only to citizens of wealthy countries
Basic rights and freedoms inherent to all people, protected in India via the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
Rights that exist only in international law with no domestic protection
Rights that only apply to government employees
questions.explanation:
Human rights are considered universal and inherent, with India providing domestic protection through the NHRC
framework established in 1993.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects correct practice for filing a consumer complaint?
options: Never keep any documentation related to purchases
Only keep documentation for purchases above ₹1 lakh
Keep receipts and evidence organised in case a consumer complaint becomes necessary
Discard your purchase receipt immediately after buying
questions.explanation: Retaining receipts and evidence strengthens your position if you need to file a consumer complaint later.

questions.question:
