Which of these best reflects why courts sometimes reference Fundamental Duties in judgments, despite them not
being directly enforceable?
options: Fundamental Duties are identical to Directive Principles with no distinction
Fundamental Duties override Fundamental Rights in all cases
Courts never reference Fundamental Duties in any context
Courts have used Fundamental Duties to help shape judgments on matters like environmental protection
questions.explanation:
Although not directly enforceable, Fundamental Duties have influenced judicial reasoning, particularly in environmental
and public interest matters.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct definition of the Right to Equality?
options: Equality before law, no discrimination, and equal opportunity
The right to own private property without any restriction
The right to a government job automatically
The right to vote exclusively
questions.explanation:
The Right to Equality guarantees equal treatment under law and prohibits discrimination, forming one of the six
categories of Fundamental Rights.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the Right Against Exploitation?
options: It guarantees free education for all ages
It prohibits human trafficking, forced labour, and child labour in hazardous work
It protects freedom of speech
It protects religious practices exclusively
questions.explanation: The Right Against Exploitation specifically prohibits practices like trafficking and forced/hazardous child labour.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects appropriate action for a citizen seeking government-held information about a delayed
public project?
options: File a consumer complaint on e-Jagriti
Contact the NHRC
File an RTI application with the relevant department
Approach the Election Commission instead
questions.explanation: RTI is the correct tool for requesting government-held information, such as project status and timeline documents.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the escalation process if an RTI request goes unanswered after 30 days?
options: No further action is possible
Simply resubmit the identical request repeatedly
Only a court case can resolve the matter
File a First Appeal, and if needed, a Second Appeal to the Information Commission
questions.explanation:
The RTI Act provides a structured appeal process — First Appeal, then Second Appeal to the Information Commission —
for unanswered requests.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct definition of "Cultural and Educational Rights" among the six Fundamental
Rights categories?
options: Protecting minorities' rights to preserve their culture and establish their own institutions
The right to bear arms
The right to unlimited free healthcare
The right to a specific salary level
questions.explanation:
Cultural and Educational Rights specifically protect minorities' ability to preserve their culture and establish educational
institutions.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects appropriate protection for a woman facing domestic violence?
options: She must resolve the matter entirely without any legal recourse
She can seek civil remedies under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
Only criminal prosecution is available with no civil remedy
No formal legal protection exists in India
questions.explanation: The 2005 Act provides specific civil remedies, including protection orders, for victims of domestic violence.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of "consumer education," one of the six consumer rights?
options: It refers to formal schooling only
It applies only to online shopping
It refers to citizens' right to be informed about their rights and responsibilities as consumers
It has no connection to consumer protection
questions.explanation: Consumer education ensures citizens understand their rights and how to exercise them effectively as consumers.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects why senior citizens might specifically benefit from knowing about the Maintenance
Tribunal?
options: It only applies to senior citizens without any children
It has no practical use for most senior citizens
It replaces the need for any government welfare scheme
It provides a formal legal avenue to claim financial support from children/relatives if neglected
questions.explanation:
The Maintenance Tribunal offers senior citizens a concrete legal remedy if they are not receiving adequate support from
their children or relatives.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct scope of the NCPCR's responsibilities?
options: Addressing child-safety concerns, including online harassment and exploitation involving minors
Managing national elections
Overseeing banking regulations
Regulating consumer product safety
questions.explanation: NCPCR specifically focuses on protecting children's rights, including addressing online safety and exploitation concerns.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of why "informed citizenship" matters, based on this module?
options: Understanding rights has no bearing on actually exercising them
Rights that aren't understood or used effectively go unused, regardless of their existence
Only lawyers need to understand citizen rights
All citizens automatically know and exercise every right without any education
questions.explanation: This module emphasises that rights are only meaningful if citizens understand and know how to exercise them in practice.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects appropriate use of the "appeal" mechanism across rights-related systems (RTI, consumer
complaints)?
options: Appeals are only available to government employees
Appeals should never be used, regardless of outcome
Using the built-in appeal mechanism when unsatisfied is a legitimate part of the process
Filing an appeal automatically results in criminal charges against the responding authority
questions.explanation:
Appeal mechanisms, like the RTI's First and Second Appeal process, are designed to be used when an initial response is
unsatisfactory.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects a "myth" about Fundamental Duties addressed in this module?
options: Fundamental Duties are listed in Part IVA
The 42nd Amendment introduced Fundamental Duties
There are 11 Fundamental Duties
Fundamental Duties are purely symbolic with no real relevance in judicial reasoning
questions.explanation:
This is a myth; courts have referenced Fundamental Duties in shaping judgments, particularly regarding environmental
and public interest matters.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects why understanding the "Right to Freedom" category matters practically?
options: It covers speech, assembly, movement, profession, and personal liberty — core everyday freedoms
It only concerns religious practices
It applies only to elected officials
It has no connection to daily civic life
questions.explanation:
The Right to Freedom encompasses core everyday liberties like speech, movement, and choice of profession that affect
daily civic life directly.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct approach when unsure whether an issue falls under consumer rights, RTI, or
human rights protections?
options: Assume no help is available and take no action

Identify the nature of the issue and match it to the correct system (e.g., consumer complaint for defective goods, RTI for
information, NHRC for rights violations)
Only ever use RTI regardless of the actual issue
File the same complaint with every possible authority simultaneously without distinction
questions.explanation:
Matching your specific issue to the correct system — as taught throughout this module — ensures your grievance reaches
the appropriate authority.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct legal position on senior citizens' right to maintenance?
options: Senior citizens have no legal recourse if children fail to support them
Maintenance rights apply only to citizens above 80 years
The Senior Citizens Act, 2007, provides a legal mechanism to claim maintenance through a Tribunal
Only a will can establish a senior citizen's right to support
questions.explanation:
The 2007 Act specifically establishes a legal mechanism — the Maintenance Tribunal — for senior citizens to claim support
from children or relatives.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the connection between Fundamental Duties and everyday "Citizen Responsibilities," as
covered in this module?
options: Citizen responsibilities have no connection to the Constitution at all
Only government employees have any civic responsibilities
They are entirely separate and unrelated concepts

Citizen responsibilities flow naturally from Fundamental Duties, like obeying laws, paying taxes honestly, and protecting
the environment
questions.explanation:
This module explicitly connects everyday citizen responsibilities to the constitutional Fundamental Duties outlined in
Article 51A.

questions.question: Considering everything in this module, what is the central lesson about Citizen Rights & Responsibilities?
options: Rights exercised responsibly, alongside duties fulfilled faithfully, are what make a democracy function well
Only rights matter; responsibilities are irrelevant to citizenship
Understanding rights and duties has no practical, real-world application
Citizens should avoid engaging with any formal rights-based systems
questions.explanation:
The module's central message is that a functioning democracy depends on citizens both exercising their rights and
fulfilling their civic duties.

questions.question: What is Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY?
options: A housing scheme for rural families
India's flagship health insurance scheme providing ₹5 lakh per family per year for hospitalisation
A scholarship programme for students
A pension scheme for senior citizens
questions.explanation: PM-JAY provides ₹5 lakh per family per year in health insurance cover, launched on 23 September 2018.

questions.question: What additional benefit did citizens aged 70+ receive under Ayushman Bharat since October 2024?
options: Free international travel insurance
A guaranteed government job
An additional ₹5 lakh cover via the Vay Vandana Card, regardless of income
Automatic voter registration
questions.explanation:
Since October 2024, all citizens aged 70 and above are universally eligible for an additional ₹5 lakh cover through the Vay
Vandana Card.

questions.question: How much does PM-KISAN provide to eligible farmer families annually?
options: ₹60,000 per year
₹600 per year
₹1 lakh per year
₹6,000 per year, in three instalments
questions.explanation: PM-KISAN provides ₹6,000 per year, paid in three instalments of ₹2,000 directly into Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts.

questions.question: What is PM Fasal Bima Yojana?
options: A crop insurance scheme protecting farmers against yield losses
A housing scheme for rural areas
A pension scheme for retired farmers
A scholarship scheme for farmers' children
questions.explanation:
PM Fasal Bima Yojana provides crop insurance against losses from natural calamities, pests, and diseases at a low farmer-
paid premium.

questions.question: What does Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) provide?
options: Housing loans at zero interest
Deposit-free LPG connections to women from poor households
Free education for girls
Free medical treatment for all citizens
questions.explanation:
PMUY, launched in May 2016, provides deposit-free LPG gas connections specifically targeting women from poor
households.

questions.question: What is Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana designed for?
options: A scheme for farmer loan waivers
A scheme for urban housing
A savings scheme for a girl child's future education/marriage expenses
A scheme for senior citizen pensions
questions.explanation:
This scheme encourages long-term savings specifically for a girl child's future needs, offering a competitive government-
set interest rate.

questions.question: What is the Atal Pension Yojana (APY)?
options: A health insurance scheme
A one-time cash grant for farmers
A scholarship for engineering students
A scheme guaranteeing a monthly pension between ₹1,000 and ₹5,000 after age 60
questions.explanation:
APY offers a guaranteed monthly pension, particularly aimed at workers in the unorganised sector, once they reach age
60.

questions.question: What is the National Scholarship Portal (NSP)?
options: A single central platform aggregating numerous central and state scholarships
A private tutoring service
A portal for university admissions exclusively
A banking platform for student loans only
questions.explanation: NSP allows students to apply for a wide range of central and state scholarships through one unified platform.

questions.question: What does MGNREGA guarantee to rural households?
options: A permanent government job
Up to 100 days of wage employment per year for unskilled manual work
Unlimited paid leave
Free housing for life
questions.explanation: MGNREGA legally guarantees up to 100 days of wage employment annually to willing rural households.

questions.question: What is PM Mudra Yojana (PMMY)?
options: A scholarship for medical students
A pension scheme for teachers
A scheme offering collateral-free loans to small entrepreneurs
A scheme providing free electricity
questions.explanation: PMMY offers collateral-free loans, typically up to ₹10 lakh (or ₹20 lakh under "Tarun Plus"), to support small entrepreneurs.

questions.question: Approximately how many loans has PM Mudra Yojana sanctioned since its 2015 launch?
options: About 1,000
Exactly 1 lakh✅ Correct Answer: Option B
About 500,000
Over 52 crore, worth more than ₹32 lakh crore
questions.explanation: PM Mudra Yojana marked 10 years in April 2025, having sanctioned over 52 crore loans worth more than ₹32 lakh crore.

questions.question: What is PM Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY)?
options: A national financial inclusion mission providing basic bank accounts
A crop insurance scheme
A scholarship for engineering students
A scheme exclusively for senior citizens
questions.explanation:
PMJDY, launched in 2014, is India's national financial inclusion mission, providing zero-balance bank accounts and RuPay
cards.

questions.question: Approximately how many bank accounts has PM Jan Dhan Yojana opened?
options: Exactly 10 crore
Over 56 crore
About 1 lakh
About 5,000
questions.explanation: PMJDY has opened over 56 crore bank accounts, with a combined deposit balance exceeding ₹2.68 lakh crore.

questions.question: What is PM Awas Yojana (PMAY)?
options: A scheme for free higher education
A pension scheme for retired government employees
A scheme providing financial assistance for pucca housing to eligible low-income families
A scheme offering free vehicles
questions.explanation:
PMAY, covering both urban (PMAY-U) and rural (PMAY-G) components, supports low-income families in securing
permanent housing.

questions.question: What is PM POSHAN, formerly known as the Mid-Day Meal Scheme?
options: A scheme for teacher training
A scheme for adult literacy
A scheme providing free textbooks only
A scheme providing hot cooked meals to school children
questions.explanation: PM POSHAN supports child nutrition and school attendance by providing hot cooked meals in schools.

questions.question: What is Samagra Shiksha?
options: An integrated scheme for school education from pre-school to senior secondary level
A scheme for adult vocational training only
A scheme exclusively for university-level education
A private tutoring company
questions.explanation:
Samagra Shiksha is the government's integrated scheme aimed at improving school effectiveness and learning outcomes
across all school levels.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)?
options: To eliminate the need for bank accounts entirely
To deliver benefits directly into a beneficiary's Aadhaar-seeded bank account, reducing leakage
To distribute cash informally without any tracking
To replace all government schemes with a single cash payment
questions.explanation: DBT ensures scheme benefits reach recipients directly and transparently, minimising the risk of leakage or diversion.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects why Aadhaar-seeding of bank accounts matters for welfare schemes?
options: Aadhaar-seeding disqualifies a person from receiving benefits
It has no real impact on scheme benefits
DBT-based schemes, like PM-KISAN, depend on Aadhaar-seeded accounts for smooth, direct payment delivery
Aadhaar-seeding is only relevant for tax purposes
questions.explanation: Without proper Aadhaar-seeding, DBT-based scheme payments can be delayed or fail to reach the intended beneficiary.

questions.question: Which of these is a common mistake citizens make regarding welfare schemes?
options: Checking eligibility on official portals
Tracking application status regularly
Applying through Common Service Centres for assistance
Paying an "agent" an unofficial fee to guarantee scheme approval
questions.explanation:
Paying unofficial fees to agents is a common and unnecessary mistake, since legitimate scheme applications are free
through official channels.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct scope of PM-KISAN eligibility?
options: It is designed specifically to support small and marginal farmer families
It is exclusively for large landowners
It applies only to farmers in one specific state
It is available only to farmers above age 70
questions.explanation: PM-KISAN is specifically designed to provide income support to small and marginal farmer families across India.

questions.question: Ramesh believes MGNREGA guarantees him a permanent job. What is the correct understanding?
options: His belief is accurate; MGNREGA guarantees lifetime employment
MGNREGA guarantees up to 100 days of wage employment per year, not permanent employment
MGNREGA only applies to urban workers
MGNREGA has been discontinued
questions.explanation:
MGNREGA specifically guarantees up to 100 days of employment annually, which is a valuable but time-limited benefit,
not permanent employment.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects a myth about Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY addressed in this module?
options: Citizens aged 70+ get additional coverage
It provides ₹5 lakh per family per year for hospitalisation
It only covers a small list of diseases with very limited application
It offers cashless treatment at empanelled hospitals
questions.explanation:
This is a myth; PM-JAY covers a wide range of secondary and tertiary treatments, though a few very high-end procedures
remain excluded.

questions.question: Which ministry primarily implements PM-KISAN?
options: Ministry of Railways
Ministry of Health & Family Welfare
Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
questions.explanation:
The Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare implements PM-KISAN, delivering income support directly to eligible farmer
families.

questions.question: Which ministry primarily implements PM Ujjwala Yojana?
options: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
Ministry of External Affairs
Ministry of Home Affairs
Ministry of Railways
questions.explanation:
The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas oversees PMUY, which provides deposit-free LPG connections to eligible
households.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct action for a family needing expensive hospital treatment they cannot afford
upfront?
options: Avoid seeking treatment altogether
Check Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY eligibility and visit an empanelled hospital for cashless treatment
Apply for PM-KISAN instead
Apply for a Mudra loan to cover medical costs
questions.explanation:
PM-JAY specifically addresses this need, providing cashless treatment up to ₹5 lakh/year at empanelled hospitals for
eligible families.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct scope of Common Service Centres (CSCs)?
options: They only provide banking services
They are private, unregulated agents

They assist citizens in applying for government schemes offline/assisted, especially those unfamiliar with online
applications
They charge high fees for every government service
questions.explanation:
CSCs provide free or low-cost assisted access to government scheme applications for citizens who may not be comfortable
applying online themselves.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of "Centrally Sponsored Schemes"?
options: Schemes with no connection to state governments at all
Schemes that apply only to central government employees
Schemes designed and funded entirely by a single state government
Schemes designed centrally but implemented jointly with states, sometimes supplemented by state top-ups
questions.explanation:
Centrally Sponsored Schemes, like Ayushman Bharat, are designed at the central level but implemented jointly with state
governments.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct scope of the Atal Pension Yojana's target group?
options: Primarily workers in the unorganised sector seeking retirement income security
Only citizens above age 80
Only urban residents
Exclusively government employees
questions.explanation:
APY is specifically designed to provide pension security for workers in the unorganised sector, who often lack formal
retirement benefits.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of "Full-KYC" versus "minimum-KYC" as it might relate to
accessing certain welfare/financial schemes?
options: Both offer identical benefits with no distinction
Full-KYC generally allows access to higher-value services, while minimum-KYC has more limited functionality
KYC status is irrelevant to any government scheme
Minimum-KYC always offers more benefits than full-KYC
questions.explanation:
KYC completion level often determines the extent of services or transaction limits available, generally with full-KYC
unlocking greater functionality.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects why "scheme awareness" is emphasised as a major theme of this module?
options: Awareness has no bearing on whether citizens receive scheme benefits
All eligible citizens automatically claim every welfare benefit they qualify for
Studies show many eligible citizens never claim benefits simply due to lack of awareness
Only wealthy citizens need to be aware of welfare schemes
questions.explanation:
This module highlights that awareness, not just eligibility, is often the biggest barrier preventing citizens from accessing
welfare benefits.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects a family's appropriate approach after learning about various welfare schemes?
options: Assume none of the schemes apply to their situation without checking
Wait for the government to automatically enrol them
Apply for every scheme regardless of relevance or eligibility
Check eligibility for relevant schemes like PM-JAY, PM-KISAN, or PMUY based on their specific circumstances
questions.explanation:
Checking eligibility for schemes relevant to a family's actual circumstances is the recommended, practical approach to
accessing welfare benefits.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct definition of PM Fasal Bima Yojana's core benefit?
options: Insurance protection against crop yield losses from natural calamities, pests, and diseases
Guaranteed employment for farmers
Free fertiliser for all farmers
Free irrigation equipment
questions.explanation:
PM Fasal Bima Yojana specifically protects farmers financially against yield losses due to unpredictable natural and
biological factors.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct scope of PM Awas Yojana's two components?
options: PMAY has no rural component at all
PMAY-U for urban areas and PMAY-G for rural (Gramin) areas
Both components serve identical purposes with no distinction
PMAY-U for farmers and PMAY-G for students
questions.explanation:
PMAY operates through two components — Urban (PMAY-U) and Rural/Gramin (PMAY-G) — tailored to different housing
needs.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct process for tracking multiple scheme applications in one place?
options: Only a lawyer can track scheme application status
Scheme tracking requires visiting a physical office each time
The UMANG app can be used alongside individual official scheme portals for tracking
There is no way to track multiple schemes together
questions.explanation:
UMANG offers a convenient way to check multiple scheme statuses alongside dedicated official portals for each specific
scheme.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects a responsible habit regarding welfare scheme communications?
options: Share personal banking details immediately upon request
Trust any message claiming to be from a scheme, regardless of source
Assume all scheme-related communication is automatically legitimate
Verify claims about eligibility or "urgent registration" independently through the scheme's official portal
questions.explanation: Independent verification through official channels helps citizens avoid falling victim to fraudulent scheme-related scams.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of why PM Mudra Yojana loans are described as "collateral-free"?
options: Small entrepreneurs can access loans without needing to pledge assets as security
Collateral-free loans are only available to large corporations
Borrowers must still provide significant collateral
"Collateral-free" means the loans are given without any application process
questions.explanation:
The collateral-free nature of Mudra loans specifically supports small entrepreneurs who may lack assets to pledge as
security.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of PM-KISAN's payment structure?
options: A single lump sum of ₹6,000 paid once every five years
Three instalments of ₹2,000 each, totalling ₹6,000 per year
A one-time payment with no recurring structure
Monthly payments of ₹500
questions.explanation: PM-KISAN disburses its ₹6,000 annual benefit in three equal instalments of ₹2,000 each throughout the year.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct scope of "social welfare programs" as a category in this module?
options: Only schemes for students
Only schemes for farmers

Broader programs like PMAY and the National Social Assistance Programme, supporting housing and vulnerable
citizens
Exclusively banking-related schemes
questions.explanation:
Social welfare programs encompass broader support systems like housing assistance and aid for elderly, widowed, or
disabled citizens.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct action for a young graduate wanting to start a small business without
collateral?
options: Apply for Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana
Apply for the Atal Pension Yojana
Apply for Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY
Explore PM Mudra Yojana for a collateral-free loan
questions.explanation:
PM Mudra Yojana is specifically designed to support small entrepreneurs with collateral-free loans, making it the
appropriate scheme for this need.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects why "scholarship amounts vary by category and education level" under the National
Scholarship Portal?
options: Different scholarship categories and educational levels have different eligibility and amount structures
Only postgraduate students are eligible for any scholarship
Scholarship amounts are determined randomly
All scholarships offer an identical fixed amount regardless of circumstances
questions.explanation:
The NSP aggregates many different scholarships, each with its own eligibility criteria and amount, tailored to specific
categories and education levels.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct definition of a "cashless service delivery" mechanism, as used in schemes like
PM-JAY?
options: Cashless delivery means the scheme has been discontinued
Benefits are delivered directly at empanelled providers without the citizen paying upfront
It refers only to online banking transactions
Beneficiaries pay upfront and get reimbursed later
questions.explanation:
Cashless service delivery, as used in PM-JAY, means eligible beneficiaries receive treatment at empanelled hospitals
without needing to pay upfront.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct scope of PM Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY)?
options: A scheme providing crop insurance
A scheme providing free housing
A scheme providing free, certified skill training to youth
A scheme providing free legal aid
questions.explanation: PMKVY focuses specifically on providing free, certified skill development training to help youth improve employability.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of why "checking eligibility even if unsure" is recommended
best practice?
options: Only wealthy citizens should check scheme eligibility
Eligibility checks are unnecessary since schemes rarely apply to anyone
Checking eligibility disqualifies you from other schemes
Many citizens assume incorrectly that a scheme "won't apply to them" and miss out on benefits they actually qualify for
questions.explanation:
This module specifically highlights that incorrect assumptions about eligibility are a common reason citizens miss out on
scheme benefits.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of "Vay Vandana Card" specifically?
options: A card providing an additional ₹5 lakh Ayushman Bharat cover for citizens aged 70 and above
A card used exclusively for voter identification
A card used for railway ticket booking
A pension card for children
questions.explanation:
The Vay Vandana Card, introduced under Ayushman Bharat, specifically extends additional health coverage universally to
senior citizens aged 70+.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of why closing dormant wallet apps might be recommended
alongside welfare scheme awareness?
options: It has no connection to welfare scheme safety
Reducing unnecessary financial app exposure is a related good practice for overall digital/financial safety
Dormant wallets automatically receive scheme benefits
Closing wallet apps disqualifies you from all government schemes
questions.explanation:
While not a scheme itself, reducing exposure through unused financial apps reflects the broader safe practices connected
to managing government benefits and finances.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct process order for accessing government scheme benefits online?
options: Submit personal details to any website mentioning the scheme name
Pay a fee first, then check eligibility afterward

Identify the relevant scheme, visit its official portal, check eligibility, complete e-KYC if required, and submit the
application
Schemes cannot be accessed online under any circumstances
questions.explanation:
This is the correct, safe sequence for accessing government schemes: identifying the scheme, verifying via official
channels, and completing necessary verification steps.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct scope of National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP)?
options: A programme exclusively for students
A programme exclusively for farmers
A programme providing free vehicles to all citizens
A programme providing pensions and support to elderly, widowed, and disabled citizens below the poverty line
questions.explanation:
NSAP specifically targets vulnerable groups — elderly, widowed, and disabled citizens below the poverty line — with
financial assistance.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of why "many schemes rely on Aadhaar" as a common thread
across welfare programs?
options: Aadhaar-based DBT is the common infrastructure enabling direct, transparent scheme delivery across many programs
Only urban schemes use Aadhaar-based delivery
Aadhaar is required only for tax purposes, unrelated to welfare
Aadhaar has no connection to welfare scheme delivery
questions.explanation:
Aadhaar-linked DBT serves as shared infrastructure across many welfare schemes, ensuring transparent and direct benefit
delivery.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of why families are encouraged to review welfare scheme
eligibility "across all categories," not just one?
options: Because reviewing multiple categories is illegal

Because checking across categories (health, farming, education, housing) can reveal benefits the family didn't realise
they qualified for
Because only one scheme category exists in total
Because families rarely qualify for more than one scheme
questions.explanation:
Given the range of welfare categories, families reviewing eligibility broadly are more likely to discover benefits they hadn't
previously realised applied to them.

questions.question: Considering everything in this module, what is the central lesson about India's government welfare schemes?
options: Welfare schemes are too complicated for ordinary citizens to access
Welfare schemes require payment of unofficial fees to access
Awareness, combined with using official channels, is the key to unlocking benefits citizens are often already entitled to
Only wealthy citizens can successfully access welfare schemes
questions.explanation:
The module's central message is that awareness and proper use of official channels — not wealth or complexity —
determine successful access to welfare benefits.

questions.question: Who typically supplies electricity to homes in India?
options: UIDAI✅ Correct Answer: Option B
The Election Commission
The Ministry of External Affairs
State-run or private Distribution Companies (Discoms)
questions.explanation: Discoms (Distribution Companies) are responsible for distributing electricity to consumers and handling billing.

questions.question: What is the Jal Jeevan Mission's core goal?
options: Providing a Functional Household Tap Connection (FHTC) to every rural home
Providing crop insurance
Building new railway lines
Distributing free mobile phones
questions.explanation:
The Jal Jeevan Mission, launched in 2019, aims to provide functional tap water connections to every rural household in
India.

questions.question: When was the Jal Jeevan Mission launched?
options: 1 July 2015
15 August 2019
26 July 2014✅ Correct Answer: Option A
23 November 2017
questions.explanation: The Jal Jeevan Mission was launched on 15 August 2019, aiming for comprehensive rural tap water coverage.

questions.question: Approximately what percentage of rural India had tap water coverage by late 2025?
options: About 50%✅ Correct Answer: Option B
About 10%
Over 81%
About 30%
questions.explanation:
Rural tap water coverage rose dramatically to over 81%, covering more than 15.72 crore households, since the mission's 2019
launch.

questions.question: What is the difference between LPG and PNG?
options: Both refer to the exact same delivery method
LPG is delivered via pipeline; PNG uses cylinders
There is no difference
LPG is a refillable cylinder connection; PNG is delivered continuously through a pipeline
questions.explanation: LPG requires periodic cylinder refills, while PNG is delivered continuously through a fixed pipeline connection.

questions.question: What does India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) primarily offer?
options: Banking services delivered through post offices and postal staff, especially in remote areas
Passport issuance
Only postal stamp sales
Airline ticket booking
questions.explanation: IPPB extends banking services to remote areas using India Post's extensive network of post offices and postal staff.

questions.question: Approximately how many post offices does India have?
options: About 500
Over 1.64 lakh
About 1,000
About 10,000✅ Correct Answer: Option B
questions.explanation: India Post operates over 1.64 lakh post offices, making it one of the most extensive postal networks in the world.

questions.question: What is a "Fair Price Shop"?
options: A discount electronics retailer
A government tax office
A shop distributing subsidised food grains under the Public Distribution System
A private grocery chain
questions.explanation: Fair Price Shops are the designated outlets where ration card holders access subsidised food grains under the PDS.

questions.question: Which portal/app is used to book Indian Railways tickets?
options: MyGov✅ Correct Answer: Option A
UMANG exclusively
DigiLocker
IRCTC
questions.explanation: IRCTC (Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation) is the primary platform for booking railway tickets in India.

questions.question: What is "Rail Madad"?
options: Indian Railways' official grievance redressal portal/app
A private railway company
A railway catering service
A type of train ticket
questions.explanation: Rail Madad allows passengers to report issues like cleanliness, security, or service problems directly to Indian Railways.

questions.question: Approximately how many passengers does Indian Railways carry on average daily?
options: About 1 lakh
About 2.3 crore
About 50 lakh
About 5,000
questions.explanation: Indian Railways carries approximately 2.3 crore (23 million) passengers daily on average, reflecting its massive scale.

questions.question: Who typically manages city bus services?
options: UIDAI
The Election Commission
State Road Transport Corporations
The Ministry of External Affairs
questions.explanation: State Road Transport Corporations are generally responsible for operating city and intercity bus services.

questions.question: Which of these is a typical municipal service?
options: Currency regulation
National defence
Passport issuance
Sanitation and waste collection
questions.explanation: Sanitation and waste collection are classic examples of services delivered by local municipal bodies.

questions.question: What is "property tax"?
options: A local tax levied by Municipal Corporations/Councils on property owners
A tax on agricultural produce
A tax on international travel
A national tax on income
questions.explanation: Property tax is levied locally by municipal bodies, funding services like roads, sanitation, and street lighting.

questions.question: Which of these is a common system used to calculate property tax?
options: Aadhaar authentication system
Annual Rental Value (ARV) system
Voter registration system
IRCTC booking system
questions.explanation:
The ARV system is one common method, alongside the Capital Value and Unit Area systems, used to calculate property
tax.

questions.question: Which scheme is credited with achieving near-universal household electrification in India?
options: Ayushman Bharat
PM-KISAN
Saubhagya scheme
Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana
questions.explanation: The Saubhagya scheme is credited with making household electricity access close to universal across Indian villages.

questions.question: What is a "smart meter," as referenced in electricity billing?
options: A type of mobile phone
A device unrelated to utility billing
A device used only for water billing
A device enabling real-time, accurate electricity billing
questions.explanation: Smart meters enable more accurate, real-time tracking of electricity consumption, improving billing accuracy.

questions.question: What is the correct process to report a water supply issue in a rural area under the Jal Jeevan Mission?
options: Report it to the local Gram Panchayat or Village Water & Sanitation Committee
Contact the Election Commission
Contact IRCTC
File an RTI request exclusively
questions.explanation:
Local bodies like the Gram Panchayat or Village Water & Sanitation Committee handle day-to-day water supply issues and
maintenance.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects a citizen's correct approach to a persistent power outage or billing dispute?
options: Assume nothing can be done about electricity issues
Contact the Discom's official helpline, app, or website for resolution and tracking
Ignore it indefinitely
Only complain informally to neighbours
questions.explanation:
Discoms provide official channels — helplines, apps, and websites — for reporting and tracking electricity-related
complaints.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct definition of ONORC in the context of PDS?
options: A scheme restricting ration cards to a single district
A private food delivery service
A scheme allowing ration card holders to access grains from any Fair Price Shop nationwide
A scheme abolishing the PDS entirely
questions.explanation:
One Nation One Ration Card (ONORC) enables portability, letting beneficiaries access their entitlements from any Fair
Price Shop in India.

questions.question:
Priya's family recently moved to a new city and is unsure who manages their new home's water/sewage connection.
Which authority should they approach?
options: The central government exclusively
IRCTC✅ Correct Answer: Option B
The Election Commission
Their local Municipal Corporation
questions.explanation: Municipal Corporations manage water and sewage connections in urban areas, making them the correct point of contact.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects why India Post's role has expanded beyond just mail delivery?
options: It now also offers Speed Post, parcel services, savings schemes, and banking through IPPB
India Post no longer delivers mail at all
India Post has been fully privatised
India Post only operates in urban areas
questions.explanation:
India Post has expanded its services significantly, combining traditional mail delivery with modern financial services
through IPPB.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct legal basis for electricity generation, distribution, and regulation in India?
options: The Aadhaar Act, 2016
The Electricity Act, 2003
The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988
The RTI Act, 2005
questions.explanation:
The Electricity Act, 2003, provides the overarching legal framework for electricity generation, distribution, and regulation in
India.

questions.question: Which law provides the legal basis for PDS entitlements?
options: The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988
The Electricity Act, 2003
The National Food Security Act, 2013
The Railways Act, 1989
questions.explanation: The National Food Security Act, 2013, establishes the legal foundation for ration card entitlements under the PDS.

questions.question: Which law governs the operation and regulation of Indian Railways?
options: The Aadhaar Act, 2016
The National Food Security Act, 2013
The Electricity Act, 2003
The Railways Act, 1989
questions.explanation: The Railways Act, 1989, provides the legal framework for the operation and regulation of Indian Railways.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct scope of "municipal governance" powers derived from the Constitution?
options: The 74th Constitutional Amendment, 1992, empowers municipal bodies to levy property tax and deliver civic services
Only the central government can levy property tax
Municipal governance has no constitutional basis
The 42nd Amendment empowers municipal bodies
questions.explanation:
The 74th Amendment specifically empowers municipal bodies with the authority to levy property tax and deliver essential
civic services.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects appropriate action for a passenger noticing unclean conditions during a train journey?
options: Wait until reaching the destination to complain
Use the Rail Madad app to report it in real time with PNR and coach details
Post about it only on social media without formal reporting
Ignore the issue entirely
questions.explanation:
Rail Madad allows real-time reporting during the journey itself, enabling faster response compared to waiting until after
arrival.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects why property tax rates and calculation methods vary across Indian cities?
options: Property tax has no variation anywhere in India
Property tax is standardised identically nationwide
Different cities/states use different systems (ARV, Capital Value, Unit Area) based on local factors
Only rural areas have property tax variation
questions.explanation:
Property tax calculation methods and rates differ by city and state, reflecting local administrative choices and property
market factors.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects a common mistake related to property tax?

questions.question: What is the maximum compensation the RBI Ombudsman can award for consequential loss?
options: There is no maximum limit
₹1 crore
₹20 lakh
questions.explanation:
The RBI Ombudsman can award up to ₹20 lakh for consequential loss, in addition to compensation for harassment or
mental anguish.

questions.question: What is the maximum additional compensation for harassment/mental anguish/time loss under RB-IOS?
options: ₹1 lakh
There is no such provision
₹50 lakh
questions.explanation:
Beyond compensation for consequential loss, the RBI Ombudsman can award up to ₹1 lakh specifically for harassment,
mental anguish, or time/expenses.

questions.question: Within how many days should a bank/NBFC respond before a customer can escalate to the RBI Ombudsman?
options: 1 year
30 days
90 days
7 days✅ Correct Answer: Option A
questions.explanation:
If a bank or NBFC doesn't respond within 30 days, or the response is unsatisfactory, the customer can escalate to the RBI
Ombudsman.

questions.question: What is the "CRPC" in relation to the RBI Ombudsman Scheme?
options: A private law firm
A type of consumer court
The Centralised Receipt and Processing Centre, RBI's intake point for Ombudsman complaints, based in Chandigarh
A banking regulator unrelated to complaints
questions.explanation: The CRPC in Chandigarh serves as RBI's centralised intake point for processing Ombudsman scheme complaints.

questions.question: What is the toll-free contact centre number for the RBI Ombudsman Scheme?
options: 181✅ Correct Answer: Option B
questions.explanation: 14448 is the toll-free number citizens can use to reach the RBI's Ombudsman contact centre.

questions.question: Within how many days can a complainant appeal an RBI Ombudsman award or rejection?
options: 30 days, to the Executive Director, CEPD
1 year
There is no appeal process
7 days
questions.explanation:
Complainants can appeal within 30 days to the Executive Director of the Consumer Education & Protection Department
(CEPD).

questions.question: What is the correct "escalation ladder" sequence recommended for resolving most grievances?
options: Formal Complaint → Direct Resolution → Appeal → Track
Direct Resolution → Formal Complaint → Track & Follow Up → Appeal/Escalate
Appeal → Track → Formal Complaint → Direct Resolution
There is no recommended sequence
questions.explanation:
This escalation ladder — direct resolution first, then formal complaint, tracking, and appeal if needed — applies broadly
across most grievance systems.

questions.question: Which system would be most appropriate for reporting a defective product and unfair trade practice?
options: CPGRAMS
RTI Online
Consumer Complaint Portal (e-Jagriti/National Consumer Helpline)
The Banking Ombudsman
questions.explanation:
Consumer product/service disputes are specifically handled through the Consumer Complaint Portal, distinct from
general government service grievances.

questions.question: Which system would be most appropriate for requesting government-held information?
options: Banking Ombudsman
Police Complaint (FIR)
Consumer Complaint Portal
RTI (Right to Information) process
questions.explanation:
RTI is specifically designed for requesting information held by public authorities, distinct from consumer or banking
grievances.

questions.question: Which system would be most appropriate for an unresolved bank service complaint after 30 days with no response?
options: Banking Ombudsman (RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme)
RTI Online
CPGRAMS
Cyber Crime Portal
questions.explanation:
Unresolved banking complaints, after the 30-day window, should be escalated specifically to the RBI's Banking
Ombudsman Scheme.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects a common mistake related to filing grievances?
options: Keeping registration/reference numbers for tracking
Filing a grievance with the wrong system out of convenience, causing delays
Attempting direct resolution first where applicable
Matching your issue to the correct system before filing
questions.explanation:
Filing with the wrong system, even out of convenience, often leads to unnecessary delays before the issue reaches the
correct authority.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects why "Zero FIR" exists as a mechanism?
options: To eliminate the need for any FIR at all
To restrict FIR filing only to the exact location where a crime occurred
To ensure a crime can be reported promptly at any police station, regardless of jurisdiction, and later transferred
To apply only to cybercrime cases
questions.explanation: Zero FIR removes jurisdictional barriers, allowing prompt initial reporting of a crime at any police station.

questions.question:
Priya's bank ignored her written complaint about a wrongly deducted charge for over a month. What is her correct next
step?
options: File a police complaint immediately
File an RTI request instead
Give up entirely on resolving the issue
Escalate to the RBI Ombudsman via cms.rbi.org.in, since more than 30 days have passed
questions.explanation:
Since the bank failed to respond within the required 30-day window, escalating to the RBI Ombudsman is the appropriate
next step.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of why matching an issue to the right system "the first time"
matters?
options: Filing with the correct system initially avoids delays caused by misrouting the complaint
All systems process complaints identically regardless of category
Only serious complaints need to be filed with the correct system
It has no bearing on resolution speed
questions.explanation:
Filing correctly the first time avoids the additional delays that occur when a complaint has to be redirected to the
appropriate authority.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct scope of "public complaint best practices" emphasised in this module?
options: Best practices are irrelevant to complaint outcomes
Being specific, attaching evidence, and using the correct category improves the chances of effective resolution
Only complaints filed in person are taken seriously
Vague complaints without evidence are equally effective as detailed ones
questions.explanation:
Specific, evidence-backed complaints filed through the correct channel are significantly more likely to be resolved
effectively.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct approach if a police station refuses to register your FIR for a cognizable offence?
options: Accept the refusal and take no further action
Assume the refusal is always justified
Escalate to a senior police officer, or approach the relevant Human Rights Commission if needed
File a consumer complaint instead
questions.explanation: Citizens have the right to escalate a wrongful FIR refusal to a senior officer or relevant human rights authority.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of "complaint tracking" across the systems covered in this
module?
options: None of these systems provide any tracking mechanism
Tracking is only available for complaints filed in person
Only banking complaints can be tracked
Each major system (CPGRAMS, e-Jagriti, RTI, cybercrime.gov.in, CCTNS, RBI CMS) issues a unique tracking number
questions.explanation:
Every major grievance system covered in this module provides a unique tracking number to help citizens follow up on
their complaint's status.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct legal basis for the RBI's Ombudsman mechanism?
options: Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949
The Aadhaar Act, 2016
The RTI Act, 2005
The Consumer Protection Act, 2019
questions.explanation: Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, provides the legal foundation for RBI's Ombudsman mechanism.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects appropriate use of the "escalation ladder" when a first response is inadequate?
options: Escalation ladders don't apply to any of these systems
Use the built-in appeal mechanism rather than abandoning the complaint
Give up immediately after one unsatisfactory response
File the exact same complaint repeatedly with no escalation
questions.explanation:
Escalation mechanisms exist precisely for situations where an initial response is inadequate, and using them is the
recommended approach.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct scope of citizen services available via the Digital Police Portal?
options: Only booking railway tickets
Only downloading tax forms
Filing FIRs/complaints, tracking status, downloading FIR copies, and requesting verifications
Only checking Aadhaar status
questions.explanation:
The Digital Police Portal offers a range of citizen services, from filing and tracking complaints to requesting various
verifications.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of why "attempting direct resolution first" is recommended
before filing a formal complaint?
options: Direct resolution is never effective and should be skipped
Direct resolution is only relevant for banking issues
Formal complaints are always faster than direct resolution
Many issues can be resolved quickly without needing formal escalation, saving time for both parties
questions.explanation:
Attempting direct resolution first can often resolve simpler issues quickly, reserving formal complaint systems for matters
that genuinely require them.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of "CISG-2025-02" in relation to the broader grievance and
cybercrime ecosystem (as covered across categories)?
options: It's a CERT-In guideline mandating cybersecurity audits, indirectly supporting a safer overall digital service ecosystem
It is a railway safety regulation
It exclusively governs banking Ombudsman procedures
It has no connection to cybersecurity or grievance systems
questions.explanation:
While primarily a cybersecurity guideline, CISG-2025-02 contributes to a safer overall ecosystem that citizens rely on for
various digital services and complaints.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of "jurisdiction-neutral" as applied to the RBI Integrated
Ombudsman Scheme?
options: The scheme applies only to complaints below ₹1,000
Customers can file complaints without worrying about which specific RBI office holds jurisdiction over their case
Complaints can only be filed in the state where the bank's headquarters is located
Jurisdiction rules make the scheme more complicated than before
questions.explanation:
The "One Nation One Ombudsman" jurisdiction-neutral approach simplifies the complaint process by removing location-
based jurisdiction barriers.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of why "matching the right system" appears repeatedly across
this module's examples?
options: It has no real bearing on complaint outcomes
Matching systems correctly is only relevant for banking complaints
It reinforces the practical skill of directing each specific type of grievance to its correct, dedicated channel
All systems are functionally identical regardless of category
questions.explanation:
This repeated emphasis reinforces the core practical skill this module teaches: correctly matching grievances to their
appropriate system.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct action if you're uncertain whether your issue is a "consumer complaint" or a
"CPGRAMS grievance"?
options: File with whichever system seems more convenient regardless of accuracy
Assume no distinction exists between the two systems
Only file with CPGRAMS regardless of the issue

Consider the nature of the issue — a defective product/service points to consumer complaint, while a general
government service issue points to CPGRAMS
questions.explanation:
Considering whether the issue relates to a private consumer transaction or a government service helps determine the
correct system to use.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct scope of NCRB's (National Crime Records Bureau) role in relation to CCTNS?
options: NCRB, under the Ministry of Home Affairs, implements CCTNS nationally
NCRB has no connection to CCTNS
NCRB exclusively handles banking complaints
NCRB only manages railway safety
questions.explanation:
NCRB, under MHA, is responsible for implementing and maintaining the CCTNS platform connecting police stations
nationwide.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects why over 99% of FIRs are now filed through CCTNS?
options: This figure reflects unrelated banking transactions, not FIRs
CCTNS has made digital FIR filing and tracking the standard, widely adopted process across India
CCTNS is used only in a handful of cities
FIRs can no longer be filed in person under any circumstances
questions.explanation:
The high adoption rate reflects CCTNS's success in becoming the standard, widely used method for FIR registration
nationwide.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct definition of "Consumer Education & Protection Department (CEPD)"?
options: A private consumer rights NGO
A department managing railway complaints
The RBI department handling appeals related to Banking Ombudsman decisions
A ministry unrelated to banking
questions.explanation: CEPD, within the RBI, specifically handles the appeal process for Banking Ombudsman Scheme decisions.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects appropriate practice for keeping records related to any of these grievance systems?
options: Discard all correspondence and reference numbers immediately
Record-keeping has no bearing on the resolution process
Only keep records for complaints exceeding ₹1 lakh
Keep all registration/reference numbers and correspondence until the issue is fully resolved
questions.explanation: Maintaining records and reference numbers until full resolution helps support any necessary follow-up or appeal.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects a citizen's correct understanding of the difference between an "NC Report" and a full "FIR"?
options: An NC Report applies to less serious matters not requiring immediate arrest, while an FIR applies to cognizable offences
FIRs can only be filed for property disputes
NC Reports are used only for banking fraud
They are identical in every respect
questions.explanation:
The distinction lies in the offence's severity — cognizable offences warrant a full FIR, while less serious matters may result
in an NC Report.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of why banks and NBFCs are given a 30-day window before RBI
Ombudsman escalation is possible?
options: To delay resolution unnecessarily for the customer
To give the regulated entity a fair opportunity to resolve the issue directly first
The 30-day window has no practical purpose
Because RBI Ombudsman complaints take exactly 30 days to process regardless of circumstances
questions.explanation:
The 30-day window ensures the bank or NBFC has a genuine opportunity to resolve the complaint before formal
escalation to the Ombudsman.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects why grievance systems in this module are described as forming "a dedicated channel so
that no citizen grievance goes without a proper channel"?
options: Only one single system handles every possible type of complaint
India lacks any structured complaint mechanisms

Each type of grievance (government service, consumer, information request, cybercrime, criminal, banking) has its own
specific, dedicated system
Citizens must resolve all grievances without any government assistance
questions.explanation: This module highlights how India has built distinct, dedicated systems tailored to different categories of citizen grievances.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of why "speed" matters in escalating a banking complaint to the
Ombudsman?
options: Speed has no bearing on Ombudsman proceedings
Complaints escalated quickly always receive higher compensation
The RBI Ombudsman only accepts complaints filed within 24 hours of an issue

While the Ombudsman process itself doesn't require the same urgency as fraud reporting, timely escalation still avoids
unnecessary delay in resolution
questions.explanation:
While not as time-critical as fraud reporting, escalating promptly once the 30-day window has passed still helps avoid
unnecessary delays in resolution.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct process for tracking an RTI application after submission?
options: Applicants can track status online and escalate via First/Second Appeal if unresolved within the 30-day window
RTI tracking requires visiting the office in person every day
RTI applications cannot be tracked once submitted
Tracking is only available for RTI requests exceeding ₹10 lakh in value
questions.explanation:
RTI applications can be tracked online, with a structured appeal process available if the 30-day response window passes
without resolution.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct scope of "banking regulation" underlying the Ombudsman Scheme's
authority?
options: It is governed entirely by the Consumer Protection Act, 2019
It draws its authority from Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949
It is based solely on informal RBI guidance with no statutory backing
The Ombudsman Scheme operates without any specific legal basis
questions.explanation:
The RBI Ombudsman Scheme's authority is grounded in the statutory power granted under Section 35A of the Banking
Regulation Act, 1949.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of "unified grievance systems" versus "specialised grievance
systems" as covered in this module?
options: All grievance systems are functionally identical
Only specialised systems exist; no unified system covers general government services

Systems like CPGRAMS handle broad government service issues, while specialised systems like the Banking
Ombudsman address specific sectors
Unified systems have completely replaced all specialised systems
questions.explanation:
This module distinguishes between broad, unified systems like CPGRAMS and sector-specific specialised systems like the
Banking Ombudsman.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct approach for a citizen filing multiple related grievances (e.g., a fraud involving
both a bank and a fraudulent website)?
options: File only one complaint and ignore the other aspects
Combined situations cannot be reported to any system
Only the police can handle such combined situations

File appropriately with each relevant system — for example, cybercrime.gov.in for the fraud and the Banking
Ombudsman for unresolved banking issues
questions.explanation:
Complex situations spanning multiple issues may require filing with more than one appropriate system to address each
aspect fully.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of why the RBI consolidated three earlier ombudsman schemes
into one in 2021?
options: To simplify and streamline banking/financial grievance redressal under a single, jurisdiction-neutral mechanism
To make the complaint process more complicated for consumers
To eliminate the ombudsman function entirely
To limit banking Ombudsman access only to businesses
questions.explanation:
Consolidating the schemes simplified the process for consumers, providing one clear mechanism instead of three
separate, potentially confusing ones.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of why "evidence" matters equally across police complaints,
consumer complaints, and banking Ombudsman cases?
options: Only written evidence is ever accepted; no digital evidence is valid
Across all these systems, clear evidence strengthens the case and supports faster, more accurate resolution
Evidence has no bearing on any of these grievance processes
Evidence is only relevant to police complaints
questions.explanation:
Regardless of the specific system, providing clear, relevant evidence consistently improves the chances of an effective and
timely resolution.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of this module's core teaching approach?
options: It introduces entirely new topics unrelated to citizen services
It replaces the need to understand any specific system in detail

It consolidates knowledge of multiple complaint systems (CPGRAMS, consumer, RTI, cybercrime, police, banking) into
one practical framework
It focuses exclusively on banking-related topics
questions.explanation:
This module's purpose is to bring together various complaint mechanisms into a single practical framework for effective
citizen use.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects why "knowing the correct escalation path in advance" is emphasised throughout this
module?
options: Only lawyers need to understand escalation paths
Escalation paths are identical across every possible situation
It has no bearing on how quickly or effectively a grievance is resolved

Knowing the path in advance allows citizens to act efficiently rather than losing time figuring out the process during an
actual grievance
questions.explanation:
Advance knowledge of the correct escalation path allows citizens to act quickly and effectively when an actual grievance
arises.

questions.question:
Considering everything in this module, what is the central lesson about government grievance and complaint systems
in India?
options:
Matching your issue to the correct system, providing clear evidence, and using tracking/appeal mechanisms together
determine successful resolution
All grievances should be handled informally without any structured system
Only wealthy citizens can effectively access these grievance systems
Grievance systems in India lack any structured escalation or tracking mechanisms
questions.explanation:
The central lesson is that success in resolving grievances depends on correctly matching the system, providing solid
evidence, and using tracking and appeal tools effectively.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution establishes the Election Commission of India?
options: Article 51A✅ Correct Answer: Option B
Article 324
Article 1
Article 32
questions.explanation: Article 324 establishes the ECI as an independent constitutional body responsible for conducting elections.

questions.question: When was the Election Commission of India established?
options: 26 November 1949
15 August 1947
25 January 1950
26 January 1950
questions.explanation: The ECI was established on 25 January 1950, a date now celebrated annually as National Voters' Day.

questions.question: What is the composition of the Election Commission of India?
options: A Prime Minister-appointed committee only
A Chief Election Commissioner alone
Five Election Commissioners
A Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners
questions.explanation: The ECI comprises a Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and two Election Commissioners, as of current structure.

questions.question: What is the minimum voting age in India?
options: 18 years
16 years
25 years✅ Correct Answer: Option B
21 years
questions.explanation: Indian citizens become eligible to vote once they reach 18 years of age.

questions.question: Which form is used for new voter registration in India?
options: Form 7
Form 6
Form 8
Form 16✅ Correct Answer: Option A
questions.explanation: Form 6 is used for registering as a new voter, or when moving to a new constituency.

questions.question: Which form is used to object to or seek deletion of an entry in the electoral roll?
options: Form 8
Form 12✅ Correct Answer: Option B
Form 7
Form 6
questions.explanation: Form 7 is used to object to an existing entry, such as for a deceased or relocated voter.

questions.question: Which form is used for correcting details within the same constituency?
options: Form 7
Form 10✅ Correct Answer: Option C
Form 6
Form 8
questions.explanation: Form 8 is used specifically for correcting existing voter details, like name spelling or address, within the same constituency.

questions.question: What is the "electoral roll"?
options: The official list of all registered voters in a constituency
A list of candidates contesting elections
A schedule of election dates
A record of Model Code of Conduct violations
questions.explanation: The electoral roll is the official register maintained by the ECI listing all eligible, registered voters in a constituency.

questions.question: What is an "e-EPIC"?
options: A physical voter ID card only
The digital version of the Electors Photo Identity Card
A railway pass✅ Correct Answer: Option B
A type of Aadhaar card
questions.explanation: e-EPIC is the digital, downloadable version of the Voter ID card, available after successful registration.

questions.question: What does the Model Code of Conduct (MCC) primarily govern?
options: Railway ticket pricing
Banking transactions during elections
The conduct of political parties and candidates during elections
School curricula
questions.explanation: The MCC sets guidelines for how political parties and candidates should conduct themselves during the election period.

questions.question: When does the Model Code of Conduct come into force?
options: Only on the day of voting
Only after the results are announced
It applies throughout the entire year, regardless of elections
Immediately upon the announcement of the election schedule
questions.explanation:
The MCC becomes effective as soon as the election schedule is announced and remains in force until the process
concludes.

questions.question: In which state's elections did the Model Code of Conduct originate?
options: Kerala, in the 1960 Assembly elections
Tamil Nadu
Uttar Pradesh
Maharashtra✅ Correct Answer: Option A
questions.explanation:
The MCC originated with Kerala's 1960 Assembly elections before being circulated nationally ahead of the 1962 Lok Sabha
elections.

questions.question: What is a VVPAT?
options: A type of voter identity card
A Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail, confirming an EVM vote via a printed slip
A political party symbol
A ballot box used before EVMs
questions.explanation: VVPAT is an attached unit that briefly displays a printed paper slip confirming the vote cast on an EVM.

questions.question: Which Supreme Court case made VVPATs a mandatory safeguard?
options: Vishaka case✅ Correct Answer: Option B
Kesavananda Bharati case
Subramanian Swamy vs Election Commission of India
Maneka Gandhi case
questions.explanation: This case established VVPATs as an indispensable requirement for ensuring free and fair elections in India.

questions.question:
How many EVMs per assembly constituency/segment are subject to random VVPAT cross-verification, following
Supreme Court directions?
options: All EVMs in every constituency
questions.explanation:
Following the N. Chandrababu Naidu case, random VVPAT verification was increased from 1 to 5 EVMs per assembly
constituency/segment.

questions.question: In April 2024, what did the Supreme Court rule regarding EVM-VVPAT verification?
options: It upheld the existing EVM-VVPAT system, rejecting 100% cross-verification or a return to paper ballots
It mandated 100% cross-verification of every EVM
It banned EVMs entirely
It transferred all election duties to state governments
questions.explanation:
The April 2024 ruling affirmed EVMs as secure and user-friendly, while directing additional safeguards rather than
mandating full manual verification.

questions.question: What is the correct order of steps at a polling booth?
options: EVM vote → ID verification → indelible ink → VVPAT confirmation
ID verification → indelible ink marking → sign/thumbprint the register → cast vote on EVM → VVPAT slip confirmation
Indelible ink → EVM vote → ID verification
VVPAT confirmation → ID verification → EVM vote
questions.explanation: This is the standard, sequential process every voter follows at a polling booth to ensure accurate, verified voting.

questions.question: What should a voter do if they believe their VVPAT slip didn't match their EVM selection?
options: Leave the booth without saying anything
Wait until after the election results to complain
Raise it immediately with the presiding officer at the booth
Nothing can be done in this situation
questions.explanation:
Prescribed procedures allow voters to raise VVPAT mismatch concerns directly with the presiding officer at the time of
voting.

questions.question: Who is India's current Chief Election Commissioner, as of 2026?
options: Sunil Arora
Om Birla✅ Correct Answer: Option A
Rajiv Kumar
Gyanesh Kumar
questions.explanation: Gyanesh Kumar became the 26th Chief Election Commissioner, assuming office on 19 February 2025.

questions.question: Approximately how many registered voters does India have?
options: Over 900 million
About 1 million
About 50 million
About 10 million
questions.explanation: India's electoral rolls include over 900 million (90+ crore) registered voters, among the largest in the world.

questions.question: Ramesh just turned 18 and wants to vote in the next election. What should he do?
options: Assume he is automatically registered
Register using Form 6 on voters.eci.gov.in
Register only through his employer
Wait until age 21 to register
questions.explanation: Voter registration requires an active application via Form 6; it does not happen automatically upon turning 18.

questions.question: Is a voter required to disclose who they voted for if asked?
options: Only if requested by a political party
Yes, it must be disclosed to authorities upon request
No, the secrecy of the ballot means voters are never obligated to disclose their vote
Only in state elections, not national ones
questions.explanation: The secrecy of the ballot is a core democratic principle, ensuring voters are never required to reveal their choice.

questions.question: What is the correct definition of "ethical voting practices," as covered in this module?
options: Voting based on payment received from a candidate
Avoiding voting altogether to remain neutral
Voting only if instructed by a family member
Voting based on informed judgement, free from inducement, coercion, or bribery
questions.explanation:
Ethical voting means casting your vote based on your own free, informed judgement, without succumbing to bribery or
coercion.

questions.question: Which Act governs the preparation of electoral rolls in India?
options: Representation of the People Act, 1950
Representation of the People Act, 1951
The Aadhaar Act, 2016
The RTI Act, 2005
questions.explanation: The Representation of the People Act, 1950, specifically governs the preparation and maintenance of electoral rolls.

questions.question: Which Act governs the actual conduct of elections in India?
options: The Electricity Act, 2003
Representation of the People Act, 1951
The Consumer Protection Act, 2019
Representation of the People Act, 1950
questions.explanation: The Representation of the People Act, 1951, governs the actual conduct and administration of elections in India.

questions.question: Which Act governs the appointment and service conditions of the CEC and Election Commissioners?
options: The Aadhaar Act, 2016
The Consumer Protection Act, 2019
The Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023
The RTI Act, 2005
questions.explanation:
This 2023 Act specifically governs the appointment process, service conditions, and term of the CEC and Election
Commissioners.

questions.question: What is the term length for the Chief Election Commissioner?
options: 2 years only
Lifetime appointment
10 years with no age limit
6 years, or until age 65, whichever comes first
questions.explanation: The CEC's term is 6 years, or until reaching age 65, whichever occurs first.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects who recommends the appointment of the CEC to the President?
options: A Selection Committee headed by the Prime Minister, including the Leader of the Opposition and a Union Minister
State Governors collectively
The outgoing CEC alone
The Chief Justice of India alone
questions.explanation:
The CEC is appointed by the President based on the recommendation of a Selection Committee that includes the PM,
Leader of Opposition, and a nominated Union Minister.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects a myth about voter registration addressed in this module?
options: BLOs may verify registration details
Turning 18 automatically registers you to vote
Voter registration requires filing Form 6
The National Voters' Service Portal handles registration
questions.explanation:
This is a myth; voter registration requires an active application, and does not happen automatically simply upon reaching
18.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects a myth about EVMs addressed in this module?
options: EVMs have been reviewed and upheld multiple times by the Supreme Court
VVPAT verification exists as a safeguard for EVMs
EVMs have never been legally reviewed by any court
The April 2024 ruling addressed EVM-VVPAT verification
questions.explanation:
This is a myth; the Supreme Court has reviewed and upheld the EVM-VVPAT system multiple times, including significantly
in April 2024.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct role of a Booth Level Officer (BLO)?
options: Issuing passports
Regulating banking transactions
Managing national election result declarations
Conducting local field verification for voter registration
questions.explanation: BLOs handle ground-level verification tasks related to voter registration within their assigned areas.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of why the MCC applies "immediately upon election schedule
announcement"?
options: To ensure a level playing field is established as soon as the electoral process formally begins
To allow parties unlimited time to prepare campaigns before any restrictions apply
The MCC actually applies only after voting concludes
The MCC has no defined start point
questions.explanation:
Applying the MCC from the schedule's announcement ensures fair conduct is maintained throughout the entire election
process.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of why India's Lok Sabha elections are described as involving
"the largest election-conducting organisation in the world"?
options: Because elections in India are conducted entirely by a private company
Because ECI deploys over a million personnel across a voter base exceeding 900 million
Because India has fewer voters than most countries
Because ECI only manages a handful of constituencies
questions.explanation:
The sheer scale of India's electorate and personnel deployment during Lok Sabha elections makes ECI's operation the
largest of its kind globally.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct action if a voter moves to a new city before an election?
options: They lose their right to vote permanently
They must wait five years before re-registering
